definition_zh: 明亮；亮度；鲜艳程度；（声音的）明亮度；聪慧
definition_en: the quality of giving out or reflecting much light, or of being vivid, clear or quick to understand
core_image: 暗室里一盏灯被调亮，光越过桌沿，照亮整个角落
scene: 灯塔守望者在深夜调大灯芯，让一束光扫过礁石。The lantern's brightness guided the fishing boats past the reef.
sceneCN: 这里指「光源发出的光的强弱」（第 1 个义项：发光体向四周送出光线的强度）；句意为灯塔灯的亮度引导渔船绕过暗礁。图中可辨识物件：灯芯、玻璃灯罩、扫过海面的光束、礁石。

pos.zh: 明亮；亮度；鲜明；（声音的）明亮度；聪慧

senses.title: Light given out by a source
senses.definition: the amount of light that a lamp, star or other source sends out
senses.definitionCN: 灯、恒星或其他光源发出的光的量
senses.example: The brightness of the lamp was too much for the small room.
senses.exampleCN: 这盏灯对这个小房间来说太亮了。
senses.why: brightness is the abstract noun of bright, so it names the quality itself rather than the thing that has it.
senses.whyCN: brightness 是 bright 的抽象名词，命名的正是「亮」这一性质，而不是发亮的物体。

senses.title: Reflected light from a surface
senses.definition: the degree to which a surface reflects light and looks light rather than dark
senses.definitionCN: 表面反射光线的程度，从而显得浅而不是深
senses.example: Fresh snow raised the brightness of the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 新雪提高了整个山谷的亮度。
senses.why: once brightness is treated as a measurable quality, it can be read off any surface, not only off lamps.
senses.whyCN: 一旦亮度被当作可测量的性质，它就能读在任何表面上，而不只属于灯。

senses.title: Vividness of a colour
senses.definition: the strength or lightness of a colour
senses.definitionCN: 颜色的强度或明度
senses.example: The restorer cleaned the canvas and the brightness of the blues returned.
senses.exampleCN: 修复师清洁了画布，蓝色的鲜艳又回来了。
senses.why: colour has its own light-like scale, so the same word moved from lamps to pigments.
senses.whyCN: 颜色本身有一套类似明暗的尺度，于是同一个词从灯移到了颜料上。

senses.title: Clearness of sound
senses.definition: the quality of a sound that is clear and high rather than dull or muffled
senses.definitionCN: 声音清晰、偏高而不沉闷含混的性质
senses.example: The new microphone added brightness to the violin's tone.
senses.exampleCN: 新麦克风让小提琴的音色更明亮。
senses.why: acoustics borrowed the visual scale: high, clean sound is called bright, and its quality is brightness.
senses.whyCN: 声学借用了视觉的尺度：高而干净的声音被称为「亮」，其性质就是 brightness。

senses.title: Apparent brightness of a star
senses.definition: the light received from a celestial body as seen from Earth
senses.definitionCN: 在地球上接收到的天体发出的光
senses.example: Astronomers recorded the brightness of the supernova every night.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家每晚记录这颗超新星的亮度。
senses.why: observers needed a word for measured light as distinct from the formal magnitude scale, and brightness filled that place.
senses.whyCN: 观测者需要一个词来指实测的光量，以区别于正式的星等标尺，brightness 正好补上这个位置。

senses.title: Screen luminance
senses.definition: the level of light set on a display or screen
senses.definitionCN: 显示器或屏幕设定的发光水平
senses.example: She lowered the brightness of her phone at night.
senses.exampleCN: 她在夜里把手机亮度调低。
senses.why: the technical sense narrowed brightness to a controllable setting on a device.
senses.whyCN: 技术义把亮度收窄为设备上一个可调节的设定值。

senses.title: Cheerful hopefulness
senses.definition: a cheerful, hopeful quality in a person or an occasion
senses.definitionCN: 人或场合中明快、充满希望的性质
senses.example: Her brightness made the long meeting feel short.
senses.exampleCN: 她的明朗让漫长的会议显得很短。
senses.why: light has long stood for happiness, so brightness carried that metaphor into mood.
senses.whyCN: 光很早就象征快乐，于是 brightness 把这层比喻带进了心情。

senses.title: Quickness of mind
senses.definition: the quality of being intelligent and quick to understand
senses.definitionCN: 聪明、理解迅速的性质
senses.example: Teachers noticed the brightness of the child in every lesson.
senses.exampleCN: 老师们在每节课上都注意到这个孩子的聪慧。
senses.why: a bright mind is one that lights up quickly, and the noun keeps that older metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 「明亮的头脑」指很快亮起来的头脑，这个名词保留了这一较早的比喻。

intro.en: Brightness is a native English formation, built from the adjective bright and the abstract suffix -ness; its root is Germanic, so it has no Latin ancestor. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: brightness 是英语本族构成，由形容词 bright 加抽象后缀 -ness 组成；其词根属日耳曼语族，没有拉丁语祖先。年代均为约数。

items.en: Old English had beorhtnes, from beorht 'shining, clear' plus the abstract suffix -nes.
items.cn: 古英语已有 beorhtnes，由 beorht「发光的、清晰的」加抽象后缀 -nes 构成。

items.en: Beorht belongs to a Germanic family represented by reconstructed *berhtaz 'bright'; the reconstruction is secure as a family label but its deeper origin is not settled.
items.cn: beorht 属于以重构形式 *berhtaz「明亮的」为代表的日耳曼语族；这一重构作为语族标签较为可靠，但其更深来源没有定论。

items.en: After the Norman period the native -nes was replaced by the borrowed -ness, giving the modern shape brightness.
items.cn: 诺曼时期之后，本族的 -nes 被借入的 -ness 取代，形成现代形式 brightness。

items.en: From the sixteenth century brightness was applied to colours, to sound and to the mind, each time keeping the idea of light.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，brightness 被用于颜色、声音与头脑，每次都保留「光」的观念。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word became a setting on screens and a measured quantity in astronomy and acoustics.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个词成为屏幕上的一个设定值，也成为天文学与声学中的可测量。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the pre-Germanic source of *berhtaz is unknown, and any Indo-European root proposed for it is a reconstruction, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：*berhtaz 在日耳曼语之前的来源不明，凡为其提出的印欧词根都是重构形式，并非已证实的派生。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root forms that are often confused with the noun; group two holds technical and near-meaning light words.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、易与这个名词混淆的形式；第二组是技术性或语义相近的光亮词。

entries.definition: The adjective that names the object which shines; brightness names the quality, so the two cannot replace each other.
entries.definitionCN: 指发亮的物体本身的形容词；brightness 命名的是性质，两者不能互换。

entries.definition: To make or become bright; it marks a change of state, while brightness is the state itself.
entries.definitionCN: 使变亮或变亮；它标记状态的变化，而 brightness 是状态本身。

entries.definition: The noun of brilliant; it adds sparkle or outstanding talent, whereas brightness is the plainer measurable quality.
entries.definitionCN: brilliant 的名词；多了闪耀或出众才华的意味，而 brightness 是更朴素、可测量的性质。

entries.definition: An adverb modifying how something shines; it answers how, not what quality is present.
entries.definitionCN: 修饰发光方式的副词；回答「怎样」，而不回答「具有什么性质」。

entries.definition: A photometric term for light emitted per unit area of a surface; it is a strict measurement, while brightness is everyday and broader.
entries.definitionCN: 光度学术语，指表面单位面积发出的光；是严格的测量量，而 brightness 日常且范围更宽。

entries.definition: The total light a star emits; brightness usually means the light actually received, so the two differ in astronomy.
entries.definitionCN: 恒星发出的总光量；brightness 通常指实际接收到的光，因此在天文学中两者有别。

entries.definition: Light as it spreads outward with warmth; it is warmer and more literary than brightness.
entries.definitionCN: 光向外扩散并带暖意；比 brightness 更温暖、更文学化。

entries.definition: The act of lighting a place or the amount of light that falls on it, rather than the light a body sends out.
entries.definitionCN: 照亮某处这一动作，或落在那里的光量，而不是某物体发出的光。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real relatives and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词后缀、真实同族词与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The suffix -ness turns the adjective bright into the abstract noun brightness.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ness 把形容词 bright 变成抽象名词 brightness。

normal.en: The family runs bright, brighten, brightly, brightening and brightness.
normal.cn: 同族形式包括 bright、brighten、brightly、brightening 与 brightness。

normal.en: Devices use brightness as a setting; astronomers use it as a measured quantity.
normal.cn: 设备把亮度当作一个设定值；天文学家把它当作可测量的量。

normal.en: Brightness is what you measure; brilliance is what you admire.
normal.cn: 亮度是量出来的；光彩是赞出来的。

normal.en: The word is Germanic, so its Latin neighbours are loanwords such as luminance and luminosity.
normal.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语族，因此它的拉丁近邻是 luminance、luminosity 一类的借词。

abstract.en: Picture a dimmer switch that slowly lifts a room out of darkness.
abstract.cn: 想象一个调光旋钮，把房间一点点从黑暗里提起来。

abstract.en: Picture light that left a star long ago still arriving at your eye.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗星很久以前发出的光，此刻才到达你的眼睛。

abstract.en: Picture a person who enters a dull room and makes it feel lighter.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人走进沉闷的房间，让整个房间轻快起来。

examples.en: The brightness of the screen was painful in the dark.
examples.cn: 屏幕的亮度在黑暗里刺眼。

examples.en: Astronomers compare the brightness of stars at known distances.
examples.cn: 天文学家比较已知距离上的恒星亮度。

examples.en: The brightness of her reply lifted the whole team.
examples.cn: 她回答时的明快让整个团队振作起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「bright（明亮）+ -ness（性质后缀）」——亮这一性质本身 → 明亮、亮度

root: 古英语 beorht「发光的、清晰的」加抽象后缀 -nes 构成 beorhtnes；bright 属日耳曼语族，与重构形式 *berhtaz 同族，更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one quality of light: it leaves a lamp, leaves a surface, colours a pigment, clears a sound, reaches us from a star, becomes a screen setting, and finally lights a mood and a mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种「光」的性质展开：它从灯发出、从表面反射、染上颜料、使声音清晰、从恒星抵达我们、变成屏幕设定，最后照亮心情与头脑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one lamp turned up in a dark room, its light reaching every corner and every surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：暗室里一盏灯被调亮，光到达每个角落与每个表面。

branches.en: MEASURED LIGHT: what a lamp or a star sends out can be compared on one scale.
branches.cn: 可量的光：灯或恒星送出的光可以放在同一把尺上比较。

branches.en: SURFACE AND PIGMENT: the quality is read off what reflects it, not only off what emits it.
branches.cn: 表面与颜料：这一性质可以从反射它的东西上读出，而不只从发光体上读出。

branches.en: CLEAR SOUND: acoustics borrows the visual scale and calls clean, high sound bright.
branches.cn: 清亮的声音：声学借用视觉尺度，把干净偏高的声音称作「亮」。

branches.en: DEVICE SETTING: a physical quantity becomes a knob the user can turn.
branches.cn: 设备设定：一个物理量变成了用户可以拧动的旋钮。

branches.en: MOOD AND MIND: light stands for cheerfulness and for quick understanding.
branches.cn: 心情与头脑：光象征明朗快乐，也象征理解迅速。

intro.en: Brightness is transparently built from an adjective plus a productive noun suffix, so its morphology can be read without guesswork.
intro.cn: brightness 由一个形容词加一个能产的名词后缀透明地构成，因此其形态可以不经猜测直接读出。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, so it has no Latin entries; the Latin layer of English supplies the technical neighbours luminance and luminosity instead.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语族，因此没有拉丁条目；英语的拉丁层改为提供 luminance 与 luminosity 这类技术近邻。

items.example: A bright star stood over the bay.
items.exampleCN: 一颗明亮的星悬在海湾上方。

items.meaning: the state or quality of being
items.example: The suffix turns an adjective into a name for its quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成其性质的名词。

items.example: The brightness of the lamp filled the room.
Dawn brightened the eastern wall.
The hall was brightly lit.

items.meaning: the act or process of becoming bright
items.example: The sky showed a slow brightening.
The overbright sign washed out the street.
items.exampleCN: 过亮的招牌把街景照得发白。

items.example: The bright-eyed child ran to the door.
items.exampleCN: 那个眼睛明亮的孩子跑向门口。

items.meaning: a graded set of brightness levels
items.example: The chart shows a brightness scale from one to ten.
items.exampleCN: 图表给出从一到十的亮度等级。

definition_zh: 巨大；重要性；量值大小；震级；星等
definition_en: great size or importance, or the size of a quantity measured on a scale
core_image: 同一把刻度尺同时量山的高度与地震的力量，标记一路向上
scene: 地震台值班员盯着纸带上跳动的曲线，把刚测到的数字写进记录表。The seismologist logged a magnitude of six point two after the tremor.
sceneCN: 这里指「地震释放能量的大小等级」（第 4 个义项：按对数标尺给出的震级数值）；句意为地震学家在震动之后记录到六点二级。图中可辨识物件：记录纸带、曲线笔、值班台、墙上的地震仪。

pos.zh: 巨大；重要性；量值；震级；星等

senses.title: Great size or extent
senses.definition: the great size or extent of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物在体积或范围上的巨大
senses.example: The magnitude of the ice sheet surprised the survey team.
senses.exampleCN: 冰盖的巨大规模让勘测队吃惊。
senses.why: Latin magnitudo named greatness in general, from magnus 'great' plus -tudo, a suffix for a state.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 magnitudo 泛指「大」，由 magnus「大的」加表状态的后缀 -tudo 构成。

senses.title: Importance or seriousness
senses.definition: the importance or seriousness of an event or problem
senses.definitionCN: 事件或问题的重要程度与严重性
senses.example: Few understood the magnitude of the decision at the time.
senses.exampleCN: 当时很少有人明白这个决定有多重要。
senses.why: greatness of size turned into greatness of consequence, so a large event is one of large magnitude.
senses.whyCN: 规模之大转而指后果之大，因此重大的事件就是 magnitude 大的事件。

senses.title: Size of a measured quantity
senses.definition: the size of a quantity expressed as a number
senses.definitionCN: 以数字表示的量的大小
senses.example: The current rises in magnitude as the resistance falls.
senses.exampleCN: 电阻下降时，电流的量值上升。
senses.why: science needed a neutral word for how large a number is, whatever its unit.
senses.whyCN: 科学需要一个中性的词来指数字本身有多大，而不论其单位。

senses.title: Earthquake magnitude
senses.definition: a number on a logarithmic scale that expresses the energy released by an earthquake
senses.definitionCN: 按对数标尺表示地震释放能量的数值
senses.example: The quake reached a magnitude of seven and toppled the old wall.
senses.exampleCN: 地震达到七级，震倒了那道旧墙。
senses.why: the general sense of measured size was fixed to the seismic scale, where each step is a large jump in energy.
senses.whyCN: 「可量的大小」这一泛义被固定到地震标尺上，那里的每一级都代表能量的大幅跃升。

senses.title: Stellar magnitude
senses.definition: a number expressing the brightness of a star, with smaller numbers for brighter stars
senses.definitionCN: 表示恒星亮度的数值，星越亮数值越小
senses.example: The faint star has a magnitude of nine and needs a telescope.
senses.exampleCN: 那颗暗星是九等，需要望远镜才能看到。
senses.why: the ancient star catalogue ranked stars by brightness, and that ranking was later kept as a reversed numerical scale.
senses.whyCN: 古代星表按亮度给星排序，这一排序后来被保留为数值越小越亮的倒序标尺。

senses.title: Length of a vector
senses.definition: the length of a vector, considered apart from its direction
senses.definitionCN: 向量的长度，不考虑其方向
senses.example: The force has a magnitude of twelve newtons and points north.
senses.exampleCN: 这个力的大小是十二牛顿，方向朝北。
senses.why: mathematics separated how much from which way, and called the first part the magnitude.
senses.whyCN: 数学把「多大」与「朝哪」分开，并把前者称作 magnitude。

senses.title: Strength of a sound
senses.definition: the strength of a sound as measured in decibels
senses.definitionCN: 以分贝计量的声音强度
senses.example: The magnitude of the noise made sleep impossible.
senses.exampleCN: 噪声的强度让人无法入睡。
senses.why: acoustics reused the measured-size sense for sound energy, again on a logarithmic scale.
senses.whyCN: 声学把「可量的规模」这一义用于声能，同样落在对数标尺上。

senses.title: Rank of importance
senses.definition: a rank or order of importance, as in a problem of the first magnitude
senses.definitionCN: 重要性的等级，如「头等重要的问题」
senses.example: They treated the leak as an issue of the first magnitude.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把这次泄漏当作头等重要的问题。
senses.why: the star scale supplied a ready idiom in which rank is expressed by magnitude.
senses.whyCN: 星等标尺提供了一个现成的说法，用 magnitude 来表达等级。

intro.en: Magnitude comes from Latin magnitudo 'greatness, size', built on magnus 'great' and the state suffix -tudo. The word entered English through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: magnitude 来自拉丁 magnitudo「巨大、规模」，由 magnus「大的」与表状态的后缀 -tudo 构成，经法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Magnus meant 'great, large, powerful'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the common link suggested to *meg- 'great' is a reconstructed root, not a proven source.
items.cn: magnus 意为「大的、广阔的、有力的」。其更深来源不确定；常被提到的 *meg-「大」是重构词根，并非已证实的来源。

items.en: Magnus plus -tudo produced magnitudo 'greatness, size, extent', a third-declension noun.
items.cn: magnus 加 -tudo 构成 magnitudo「巨大、规模、范围」，是第三变格法名词。

items.en: Old French magnitude carried the word into English in the fourteenth century, first as a general term for greatness.
items.cn: 古法语 magnitude 在十四世纪把该词带入英语，最初泛指「巨大」。

items.en: From the seventeenth century magnitude was used for the size of a measurable quantity, especially in astronomy.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，magnitude 被用于可测量量的大小，尤其在天文学中。

items.en: The seismological sense dates from the twentieth century, when magnitude was fixed to a logarithmic energy scale.
items.cn: 地震学义始于二十世纪，当时 magnitude 被固定到对数能量标尺上。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): magnus has no established Indo-European ancestor, and any form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：magnus 没有已确定的印欧祖先，凡为其提出的形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin root that look alike but mean different things; group two holds near-meaning size words.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词根、形近而义异的词；第二组是语义相近的「大小」词。

entries.definition: From magnus plus -ficare 'to make': to make something appear larger, not to be large itself.
entries.definitionCN: 由 magnus 加 -ficare「使」构成：使某物看起来更大，而不是自身巨大。

entries.definition: Magnus plus -ficent 'doing': splendid in appearance, close to grand rather than to measurable size.
entries.definitionCN: magnus 加 -ficent「做」：外观壮丽，接近「宏伟」，而非可测的规模。

entries.definition: Magnus plus animus 'mind': great-souled, generous, with nothing to do with physical size.
entries.definitionCN: magnus 加 animus「心」：心胸宏大的、宽厚的，与物理大小无关。

entries.definition: A graded set of numbers for brightness or energy; the compound names the instrument, while magnitude names the number.
entries.definitionCN: 表示亮度或能量的分级数值体系；复合词指这套标尺，而 magnitude 指其中的数值。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for how large a thing is; magnitude is its formal and technical counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指物体有多大的日常词；magnitude 是其正式、技术化的对应词。

entries.definition: The degree to which something covers an area or reaches a limit, stressing spread rather than bulk.
entries.definitionCN: 某物覆盖面积或达到界限的程度，强调铺展而非体积。

entries.definition: The level at which something operates, as on a scale from small to large; magnitude is the reading on that scale.
entries.definitionCN: 事物运作的相对层级，如由小到大的标尺；magnitude 是标尺上的读数。

entries.definition: The harshness or seriousness of something bad; it adds the idea of harm that magnitude alone does not carry.
entries.definitionCN: 坏事之严酷或严重；多了「造成伤害」的意思，而 magnitude 本身不含此意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin morphemes and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁语素与真实固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: magnus 'great' plus -tudo 'state' gives 'state of being great'.
normal.cn: magnus「大」加 -tudo「状态」即「大的状态」。

normal.en: Order of magnitude marks a jump of about ten times.
normal.cn: 数量级标记约十倍的跃升。

normal.en: Earthquake magnitude and stellar magnitude are both logarithmic scales.
normal.cn: 震级与星等都是对数标尺。

normal.en: Of the first magnitude means of the highest rank.
normal.cn: 头等重要的，即最高等级。

normal.en: The family runs magnitude, magnify, magnificent, magnification, magnanimous.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 magnitude、magnify、magnificent、magnification、magnanimous。

abstract.en: Picture one ruler long enough to measure both a mountain and a quake.
abstract.cn: 想象一把足够长的尺，既能量山，也能量地震。

abstract.en: Picture a star chart where the brightest star is given the smallest number.
abstract.cn: 想象一张星图，最亮的星反倒标着最小的数字。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour that grows until nobody can ignore its size.
abstract.cn: 想象一个传闻越滚越大，大到没人能忽视。

examples.en: Nobody grasped the magnitude of the loss until the accounts were closed.
examples.cn: 直到账目结清，人们才明白损失有多大。

examples.en: Each step on the magnitude scale means roughly thirty times more energy.
examples.cn: 震级标尺上的每一级大约意味着三十倍的能量。

examples.en: The magnitude of the vector is independent of its direction.
examples.cn: 向量的大小与其方向无关。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「magni（大）+ tude（状态）」——大的状态就是「巨大、规模、量值」

root: 拉丁 magnus「大的」+ -tudo（表状态）→ magnitudo「巨大、规模」，经法语 magnitude 进入英语；magnus 更深来源不确定，*meg- 一说是重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all measure how much: bulk, consequence, number, seismic energy, starlight, vector length, sound and rank.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在量「有多大」：体积、后果、数值、地震能量、星光、向量长度、声音与等级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single ruler marked from small to great, laid first against a mountain and then against a quake.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把由小到大的刻度尺，先量山，再量地震。

branches.en: SIZE AND WEIGHT: what is physically large becomes socially serious.
branches.cn: 体积与分量：物理上的大转化为社会意义上的重。

branches.en: NUMBER ON A SCALE: any measured strength can be read as a number.
branches.cn: 标尺上的数：任何可测的强度都能读成一个数。

branches.en: SEISMIC SCALE: the number is fixed to a logarithmic energy ladder.
branches.cn: 地震标尺：这个数被固定到对数能量阶梯上。

branches.en: STELLAR RANK: brightness becomes rank, and rank becomes an idiom.
branches.cn: 星等与等级：亮度变成等级，等级又变成成语。

branches.en: LENGTH ALONE: direction is stripped away, leaving pure size.
branches.cn: 只剩长度：方向被剥离，留下纯然的大小。

intro.en: Magnitude is one Latin root plus one state suffix, and that root also builds several common English words.
intro.cn: magnitude 是一个拉丁词根加一个状态后缀，这个词根还构成若干常用英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin magnus 'great' gives magnitude, magnify, magnificent and magnanimous; -tudo marks a state or quality.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 magnus「大」衍生 magnitude、magnify、magnificent 与 magnanimous；-tudo 标记状态或性质。

items.example: Magnus is the root behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: magnus 是整个词族的词根。

items.example: The suffix turns an adjective into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成表状态的名词。

items.example: The magnitude of the task was clear.
The lens magnifies the print.
The hall was magnificent.
The magnificence of the view silenced them.
items.exampleCN: 景色的壮丽让他们说不出话。

items.meaning: the act or degree of enlarging
items.example: The microscope has ten times magnification.
items.exampleCN: 这台显微镜有十倍放大。

items.example: He read the fine print with a magnifier.
She was magnanimous in victory.

latinEntries.structure: magnus, magna, magnum (adj., first and second declension)

definition_zh: 恒星星等；表示恒星亮度的对数标尺数值
definition_en: a number on a logarithmic scale that expresses how bright a star appears or how much light it truly emits
core_image: 夜空里一排星点旁标着由负到正的刻度，越亮的星数字越小
scene: 天文台圆顶里，观测者把同一片星场拍下来，逐颗比对亮度，写下每颗星的等级。The chart lists the stellar magnitude of every star in the cluster.
sceneCN: 这里指「用对数标尺表示恒星亮度的数值」（第 1 个义项：视星等，数值越小表示越亮）；句意为星图列出这个星团中每颗恒星的星等。图中可辨识物件：星图、圆顶、望远镜、铅笔记录。

pos.zh: 恒星星等（可数，复数为 stellar magnitudes）

senses.title: Apparent brightness rank of a star
senses.definition: the rank of a star's brightness as seen from Earth, with smaller numbers for brighter stars
senses.definitionCN: 从地球看到的恒星亮度等级，星越亮数值越小
senses.example: The chart lists the stellar magnitude of every star in the cluster.
senses.exampleCN: 星图列出这个星团中每颗恒星的星等。
senses.why: stellar supplies the object and magnitude supplies the ranked number, so the phrase reads as the brightness rank of a star.
senses.whyCN: stellar 提供对象，magnitude 提供等级数值，因此整个短语读作「恒星的亮度等级」。

senses.title: Absolute brightness rank
senses.definition: the brightness a star would have if placed at a standard distance of ten parsecs
senses.definitionCN: 把恒星放在十秒差距的标准距离上时它应有的亮度
senses.example: Absolute stellar magnitude removes distance from the comparison.
senses.exampleCN: 绝对星等把距离因素从比较中剔除。
senses.why: the adjective absolute marks a value freed from the observer's position, while the base term still means ranked brightness.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 absolute 标记一个脱离观测位置的值，而基本术语仍指分级的亮度。

senses.title: The logarithmic scale itself
senses.definition: the five-step logarithmic system in which a difference of five magnitudes equals a factor of one hundred in brightness
senses.definitionCN: 五级一档的对数体系，星等相差五级即亮度相差一百倍
senses.example: On the stellar magnitude scale, a difference of five means a hundredfold change.
senses.exampleCN: 在星等标尺上，相差五级意味着亮度变化一百倍。
senses.why: the phrase can name not just a reading but the ladder the reading sits on.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语不仅可以指一个读数，也可以指读数所在的那把梯子。

senses.title: Negative magnitude for very bright objects
senses.definition: a magnitude below zero, assigned to objects brighter than the zero point such as Venus or Sirius
senses.definitionCN: 低于零的星等，赋给比零点更亮的天体，如金星或天狼星
senses.example: Sirius carries a negative stellar magnitude in most modern catalogues.
senses.exampleCN: 在多数现代星表里，天狼星的星等为负。
senses.why: because the scale was built backwards, the brightest objects fall below zero and take negative numbers.
senses.whyCN: 由于标尺是倒着建立的，最亮的天体会落到零以下，取负值。

senses.title: Magnitude difference and flux ratio
senses.definition: the numerical gap between two magnitudes, from which the ratio of received light is calculated
senses.definitionCN: 两个星等之间的数值差，据此算出来光量的比值
senses.example: A stellar magnitude difference of one corresponds to about two and a half times the light.
senses.exampleCN: 星等相差一级，约对应两点五倍的光量。
senses.why: the scale is logarithmic, so subtraction on the magnitude side becomes division on the light side.
senses.whyCN: 标尺是对数的，因此在星等一侧做减法，相当于在光量一侧做除法。

senses.title: Photometric magnitude in a band
senses.definition: a magnitude measured through a specified filter or wavelength band
senses.definitionCN: 通过特定滤光片或波段测得的星等
senses.example: The survey reports a stellar magnitude in the red band for each source.
senses.exampleCN: 巡天为每个源给出红波段的星等。
senses.why: instruments do not see all wavelengths at once, so the phrase is qualified by the band being measured.
senses.whyCN: 仪器不能一次看见所有波长，因此这个短语要用所测波段来限定。

senses.title: A value kept in a star catalogue
senses.definition: a published magnitude recorded in a catalogue and reused by later observers
senses.definitionCN: 记录在星表中、供后来观测者沿用的星等
senses.example: The old stellar magnitude in the catalogue was half a step too bright.
senses.exampleCN: 星表里的旧星等偏亮了半级。
senses.why: catalogues preserve numbers across centuries, so the phrase also names a historical record.
senses.whyCN: 星表把数字保存数百年，因此这个短语也指一份历史记录。

senses.title: Figurative rank of importance
senses.definition: a borrowed use in which people or events are ranked like stars on the brightness scale
senses.definitionCN: 借用星等标尺给人或事件排出的重要等级
senses.example: In the world of violin making, he is of the first stellar magnitude.
senses.exampleCN: 在小提琴制作界，他属于第一等。
senses.why: the reversed scale became an idiom of rank, and the adjective stellar adds the sense of excellence.
senses.whyCN: 这套倒序标尺成了表示等级的说法，而形容词 stellar 又添上「卓越」之意。

intro.en: Stellar magnitude joins Latin stellaris 'of stars' to Latin magnitudo 'greatness'. The technical sense was fixed by astronomers in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: stellar magnitude 把拉丁 stellaris「星的」与拉丁 magnitudo「巨大」连接起来；这一技术义由十九世纪的天文学家固定。年代均为约数。

items.en: Stella 'star' produced stellaris 'of stars'. The deeper origin of stella is uncertain; the link to a reconstructed *ster- 'star' is a hypothesis shared with Greek aster.
items.cn: stella「星」构成 stellaris「星的」。stella 更深来源不确定；与重构词根 *ster-「星」的联系只是与希腊语 aster 共享的假说。

items.en: Magnitudo 'greatness, size' came from magnus 'great' plus -tudo, a state suffix.
items.cn: magnitudo「巨大、规模」来自 magnus「大的」加表状态的后缀 -tudo。

items.en: Greek and later Arabic star lists sorted stars into six brightness classes, the practice that gave magnitude its astronomical sense.
items.cn: 希腊与后来的阿拉伯星表把恒星分成六个亮度等级，这一做法赋予 magnitude 天文学含义。

items.en: Photometry made the old classes numerical and logarithmic, and the phrase stellar magnitude settled into its modern meaning.
items.cn: 测光学使旧的等级变成数值与对数关系，stellar magnitude 这一短语也固定为现代含义。

items.en: Twentieth-century surveys added band-specific magnitudes and absolute magnitudes, extending the phrase rather than replacing it.
items.cn: 二十世纪的巡天增添了分波段星等与绝对星等，扩展了这一短语而非取代它。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): both stella and magnus lack established Indo-European ancestors, so the roots often printed for them are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：stella 与 magnus 都没有已确定的印欧祖先，常为它们印出的词根均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the magnitude labels that are routinely swapped; group two holds words for brightness and light output.
note.cn: 第一组是常被互换的星等标签；第二组是表示亮度与光输出的词。

entries.definition: The brightness actually seen from Earth, which includes the effect of distance; stellar magnitude alone does not say which value is meant.
entries.definitionCN: 从地球实际看到的亮度，包含距离影响；单说 stellar magnitude 并未指明是哪一种值。

entries.definition: The brightness a star would show at ten parsecs, used to compare true luminosity.
entries.definitionCN: 恒星在十秒差距处应有的亮度，用于比较真实光度。

entries.definition: A magnitude integrated over the whole spectrum, not through one band.
entries.definitionCN: 在整个光谱上积分的星等，而非通过某一波段测得。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of stars'; it cannot stand alone for the number, which is the magnitude.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「恒星的」的形容词；它不能单独指那个数值，数值由 magnitude 承担。

entries.definition: The actual amount of light received; magnitude is the rank assigned on a logarithmic scale.
entries.definitionCN: 实际接收到的光量；magnitude 是在对数标尺上赋予的等级。

entries.definition: The total energy a star radiates per second, an intrinsic physical quantity rather than a rank.
entries.definitionCN: 恒星每秒辐射的总能量，是内禀物理量而非等级。

entries.definition: The energy arriving per unit area per unit time; it is the physical input from which a magnitude is calculated.
entries.definitionCN: 单位面积单位时间到达的能量；是由它算出星等的物理输入。

entries.definition: The light level as observed, without converting it into the magnitude scale.
entries.definitionCN: 观测到的光量水平，尚未换算成星等标尺。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real astronomical usage and real Latin pieces, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的天文用法与真实的拉丁成分，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Smaller number, brighter star: the scale runs backwards.
normal.cn: 数字越小，星越亮：这套标尺是倒着的。

normal.en: Five magnitudes equal a hundredfold change in brightness.
normal.cn: 五个星等等于亮度一百倍的变化。

normal.en: Apparent magnitude includes distance; absolute magnitude removes it.
normal.cn: 视星等包含距离；绝对星等排除距离。

normal.en: The phrase is stellar (of stars) plus magnitude (ranked size).
normal.cn: 这个短语是 stellar「星的」加 magnitude「分级大小」。

normal.en: Of the first magnitude survives as an idiom of rank.
normal.cn: 头等重要的说法作为表示等级的成语留存下来。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder where the top rung is labelled with the smallest number.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子，最上面那级标着最小的数字。

abstract.en: Picture two lamps, one near and one far, looking equally bright to your eye.
abstract.cn: 想象两盏灯，一近一远，在你眼里却一样亮。

abstract.en: Picture a night sky sorted into ranks by a patient ancient observer.
abstract.cn: 想象一位耐心的古代观测者把夜空分成等级。

examples.en: The telescope reaches stars of stellar magnitude fourteen.
examples.cn: 这台望远镜能观测到十四等的恒星。

examples.en: Astronomers converted the old stellar magnitude into a modern flux measurement.
examples.cn: 天文学家把旧星等换算成现代的光通量测量值。

examples.en: Her reputation in the field is of the first stellar magnitude.
examples.cn: 她在这一领域的声望属第一等。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「stellar（恒星的）+ magnitude（等级数值）」——给恒星亮度排出的等级 → 星等

root: 拉丁 stellaris「星的」来自 stella「星」，其更深来源不确定；拉丁 magnitudo「巨大」来自 magnus「大的」加 -tudo（状态）。stella 与 magnus 的印欧词根均属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one number: it ranks a star as seen, as it truly is, as a scale, below zero, as a difference, through a filter, as a catalogue entry and finally as a human rank.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个数值：它给恒星排出视亮度、真实亮度、标尺本身、零下取值、差值、波段读数、星表记录，最后是人的等级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a night sky graded by a reversed ruler, the brightest star carrying the smallest mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：夜空被一把倒置的尺子分级，最亮的星带着最小的刻度。

branches.en: A RANK AND A LADDER: one reading and the system that produces it.
branches.cn: 等级与梯子：一个读数，以及产生它的体系。

branches.en: DISTANCE REMOVED: the same rank recalculated at a standard distance.
branches.cn: 去掉距离：同一等级在标准距离上重算。

branches.en: BELOW ZERO AND ON PAPER: bright objects go negative, and catalogues keep the number.
branches.cn: 零下与纸上：极亮天体取负值，星表把数字留存。

branches.en: DIFFERENCE AND BAND: subtraction on the scale, measurement through a filter.
branches.cn: 差值与波段：标尺上做减法，滤光片里做测量。

branches.en: HUMAN RANK: the star scale becomes a way of grading people.
branches.cn: 人的等级：星等标尺变成给人分级的方式。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin adjective of stars to a Latin noun of greatness, so both halves carry recognisable relatives.
intro.cn: 这个短语把表示「星的」拉丁形容词与表示「巨大」的拉丁名词连接起来，两半都有可辨认的同族词。

latinIntro.en: Stella and stellaris supply the first half; magnus, magnitudo and -tudo supply the second.
latinIntro.cn: stella 与 stellaris 提供前半；magnus、magnitudo 与 -tudo 提供后半。

items.example: Stella is the root of stellar and interstellar.
items.exampleCN: stella 是 stellar 与 interstellar 的词根。

items.example: Stellaris gives the English stellar.
Stellar light takes years to reach us.
items.exampleCN: 星光要多年才到达我们。

items.example: Magnus is the root of magnitude.
items.exampleCN: magnus 是 magnitude 的词根。

items.example: The suffix builds nouns of state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表状态的名词。

items.example: The magnitude of the star was recorded.
items.exampleCN: 这颗星的星等被记录下来。

items.example: Dust clouds fill interstellar space.
The lens magnifies the star's image.
The poem describes a stelliferous sky.
items.exampleCN: 这首诗描写布满星辰的夜空。

items.example: The magnitude scale runs in reverse.

definition_zh: 红移；光谱线整体向长波方向的移动
definition_en: the displacement of spectral lines toward longer wavelengths, caused by motion, gravity or the expansion of space
core_image: 一束白光穿过棱镜散成光谱，谱线整体向红色一端滑过去
scene: 天文台深夜的屏幕上，一条吸收线离开了实验室里的位置，往红色那端偏了一小段。The spectra of distant galaxies show a clear redshift that grows with distance.
sceneCN: 这里指「谱线整体向长波一端移动的现象」（第 1 个义项：波长被拉长、频率降低）；句意为遥远星系的光谱显示出随距离增大的明显红移。图中可辨识物件：光谱屏、吸收线、棱镜、观测窗。

pos.zh: 红移；向长波方向的谱线位移

collocations.phrase: a redshift of zero point one

senses.title: Spectral lines moved toward red
senses.titleCN: 谱线整体向长波一端移动
senses.definition: the shift of spectral lines to longer wavelengths and lower frequencies
senses.definitionCN: 谱线向更长波长、更低频率的移动
senses.example: The spectra of distant galaxies show a clear redshift that grows with distance.
senses.exampleCN: 遥远星系的光谱显示出随距离增大的明显红移。
senses.why: red names the end of the visible spectrum toward which the lines slide, and shift names the displacement itself.
senses.whyCN: red 指谱线滑向的可见光谱那一端，shift 指位移本身。

senses.title: Doppler redshift from receding motion
senses.titleCN: 退行运动造成的多普勒红移
senses.definition: the redshift produced when a source moves away from the observer
senses.definitionCN: 光源远离观测者时产生的红移
senses.example: The star's redshift reveals that it is moving away from us.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗星的红移表明它正在远离我们。
senses.why: a receding source stretches the waves it sends, so the physical cause is motion rather than colour.
senses.whyCN: 远离的光源把发出的波拉长，因此其物理成因是运动，而非颜色。

senses.title: Cosmological redshift from expanding space
senses.titleCN: 空间膨胀造成的宇宙学红移
senses.definition: the redshift produced because the space through which the light travels has expanded
senses.definitionCN: 光在传播过程中所经过的空间膨胀所造成的红移
senses.example: Cosmological redshift is read as a measure of how much space has stretched.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙学红移被读作空间拉伸程度的量度。
senses.why: in an expanding universe the wave itself is stretched in transit, so distance adds to the effect.
senses.whyCN: 在膨胀的宇宙中，波在旅途中本身就被拉长，因此距离会叠加到这一效应上。

senses.title: Gravitational redshift
senses.definition: the redshift of light climbing out of a strong gravitational field
senses.definitionCN: 光从强引力场中爬出时产生的红移
senses.example: Light from the dense star showed a gravitational redshift.
senses.exampleCN: 来自那颗致密恒星的光显示出引力红移。
senses.why: light loses energy escaping a deep well, and lower energy appears at longer wavelength.
senses.whyCN: 光逃离深引力势阱时损失能量，能量变低就表现为波长变长。

senses.title: The measured redshift value
senses.definition: the number z that records the fractional change in wavelength
senses.definitionCN: 记录波长相对变化量的数值 z
senses.example: The quasar has a redshift above six, far beyond nearby galaxies.
senses.exampleCN: 这个类星体的红移超过六，远大于近邻星系。
senses.why: astronomers needed a compact symbol for the amount of shift, and the word took over the value itself.
senses.whyCN: 天文学家需要一个紧凑的符号表示位移量，这个词便转而指这个数值。

senses.title: Redshift as a distance gauge
senses.definition: the use of redshift to estimate the distance of a remote object
senses.definitionCN: 用红移估计遥远天体距离的做法
senses.example: The team used redshift to place the galaxy on the distance ladder.
senses.exampleCN: 团队用红移把这个星系放到距离阶梯上。
senses.why: because expansion links stretch to distance, a measured shift becomes a ruler.
senses.whyCN: 由于膨胀把拉伸与距离联系起来，测得的位移就成了尺子。

senses.title: A redshift survey
senses.definition: a systematic observation that records redshifts for many objects at once
senses.definitionCN: 一次系统观测，同时记录大量天体的红移
senses.example: The redshift survey mapped thousands of galaxies in a narrow strip.
senses.exampleCN: 这项红移巡天在一条窄带内测绘图了数千个星系。
senses.why: the mass measurement of shifts gave its name to the whole observing programme.
senses.whyCN: 大规模测量位移的做法，把名字给了整个观测计划。

senses.title: Figurative stretching or delay
senses.definition: a borrowed use for any signal that arrives stretched, weakened or delayed
senses.definitionCN: 借指任何到达时被拉长、减弱或延后的信号
senses.example: The old recording has a kind of redshift: everything arrives slower and lower.
senses.exampleCN: 那段旧录音有种红移感：一切都来得更慢、更低。
senses.why: the physical stretching of waves became an image for anything that reaches us worn thin.
senses.whyCN: 波被物理拉长，成了任何抵达时已被磨薄的事物的意象。

intro.en: Redshift is an English compound coined in astronomy, joining red and shift. It has no Latin ancestor. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: redshift 是英语复合词，由 red 与 shift 构成，在天文学中造出，没有拉丁语祖先。年代均为约数。

items.en: Red goes back to Old English read 'red', and shift to sciftan 'to arrange, divide'; both are Germanic.
items.cn: red 可追溯到古英语 read「红的」，shift 可追溯到 sciftan「安排、分配」；两者都属日耳曼语族。

items.en: The compound was formed in the early twentieth century, when astronomers needed a short name for lines moving toward the red end.
items.cn: 这个复合词在二十世纪初形成，当时天文学家需要一个短名来指谱线朝红端移动。

items.en: After the late 1920s the redshift of galaxies was tied to cosmic expansion, and the word became central to cosmology.
items.cn: 二十世纪二十年代后期以后，星系红移被与宇宙膨胀联系起来，这个词成为宇宙学的核心术语。

items.en: Large redshift surveys from the 1970s onward turned the word into a name for an entire observing method.
items.cn: 从二十世纪七十年代起，大规模红移巡天把这个词变成了整种观测方法的名称。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the exact first printed use of the compound is not fixed, and the pre-Germanic origin of both parts is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：这个复合词确切的最早印刷用例没有定论，两个成分在日耳曼语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds the look-alike shift terms that are constantly swapped; group two holds words for the light change itself.
note.cn: 第一组是常被互换的形近位移术语；第二组是表示光变化本身的词。

entries.definition: The same displacement toward shorter wavelengths, caused by approach or by light falling into a gravity well.
entries.definitionCN: 同一类位移，但朝更短波长，由接近运动或光落入引力势阱造成。

entries.definition: The dimming and colouring of starlight by interstellar dust; lines do not move, so it is not a redshift.
entries.definitionCN: 星际尘埃使星光变暗变红；谱线并不移动，因此不是红移。

entries.definition: The participial adjective describing light whose lines have already moved; it names a state, not the phenomenon.
entries.definitionCN: 分词形容词，描述谱线已经移动的光；它指状态，而非现象本身。

entries.definition: Any displacement; redshift adds the direction and the spectral setting.
entries.definitionCN: 任何位移；redshift 增添了方向与光谱语境。

entries.definition: The general frequency change from relative motion, of which redshift is the long-wavelength case.
entries.definitionCN: 相对运动造成的一般频率变化，红移是其中长波的一端。

entries.definition: The growth of space itself that stretches light in transit; redshift is the observable result.
entries.definitionCN: 空间本身的增长，使光在途中被拉长；红移是可观测的结果。

entries.definition: A dark or bright line at a fixed wavelength; redshift is read from where that line now sits.
entries.definitionCN: 固定波长处的暗线或亮线；红移由这条线现在的位置读出。

entries.definition: The distance between wave crests; a redshift is an increase in this distance.
entries.definitionCN: 波峰之间的距离；红移就是这一距离的增加。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real parts, real instruments and real survey usage, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实仪器与真实巡天用法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Red plus shift: the lines slide toward the red end.
normal.cn: 红色加位移：谱线滑向红端。

normal.en: Receding sources redshift; approaching sources blueshift.
normal.cn: 远离的光源红移；接近的光源蓝移。

normal.en: Cosmological, Doppler and gravitational are the three standard causes.
normal.cn: 宇宙学、多普勒与引力是三种标准成因。

normal.en: Redshift is written as z and grows with distance in an expanding universe.
normal.cn: 红移写作 z，在膨胀宇宙中随距离增大。

normal.en: A redshift survey records z for thousands of galaxies at once.
normal.cn: 红移巡天一次记录数千个星系的 z 值。

abstract.en: Picture a painted line on a rubber sheet, stretched as the sheet grows.
abstract.cn: 想象橡胶布上画着一条线，布一拉长，线也跟着被拉长。

abstract.en: Picture a siren falling in pitch as the ambulance pulls away.
abstract.cn: 想象救护车远去时警笛的音调下沉。

abstract.en: Picture a letter that arrives longer and fainter than it was written.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信寄到时比写时更长、更淡。

examples.en: The galaxy's redshift places it billions of light years away.
examples.cn: 这个星系的红移把它定在数十亿光年之外。

examples.en: Gravitational redshift was measured in light from a white dwarf.
examples.cn: 引力红移在白矮星的光中被测到。

examples.en: The survey plots redshift against position on the sky.
examples.cn: 这项巡天把红移对天空位置作图。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「red（红）+ shift（移动）」——谱线整体往红端移动 → 红移

root: 英语本族复合词，由 red（古英语 read）与 shift（古英语 sciftan）构成，二十世纪初在天文学中造出，无拉丁同族，拉丁条目数组留空；两个成分的日耳曼语之前来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one displacement: lines slide red, a source recedes, space stretches, gravity pulls, a number is read, a distance is inferred, a survey is named and finally any signal arrives worn thin.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一次位移：谱线向红端滑、光源退行、空间拉伸、引力作用、读出数值、推得距离、命名巡天，最后是任何信号抵达时已被磨薄。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spectrum drawn on a rubber band that is quietly stretched from the blue end.
core.cn: 核心意象：画在橡皮筋上的光谱，被从蓝端悄悄拉长。

branches.en: LONGER WAVE: motion away stretches what is sent.
branches.cn: 更长的波：远离的运动把发出的波拉长。

branches.en: EXPANDING SPACE: the stretching happens in transit, not at the source.
branches.cn: 膨胀空间：拉伸发生在旅途中，而非在光源处。

branches.en: GRAVITY WELL: energy lost while climbing shows up as longer wavelength.
branches.cn: 引力势阱：爬升时损失的能量表现为更长的波长。

branches.en: NUMBER AND RULER: the shift is read as z, and z is read as distance.
branches.cn: 数值与尺子：位移读成 z，z 又读成距离。

branches.en: PROGRAMME AND METAPHOR: a survey is named after it, and any stretched signal borrows it.
branches.cn: 计划与比喻：巡天以它命名，任何被拉长的信号也借用它。

intro.en: Redshift is a two-word English compound, so each half can be read on its own, but neither half is Latin.
intro.cn: redshift 是由两个英语词构成的复合词，两半都能单独读出，但两半都不是拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: There are no Latin entries for this word: both parts are Germanic, and the Latin layer of astronomy supplies only loanwords such as spectrum.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁条目：两部分都属日耳曼语族，天文学的拉丁层只提供「光谱」一类的借词。

items.example: The line sits at the red end.
The line shifted by a small amount.
The galaxy's redshift is easy to measure.
items.exampleCN: 这个星系的红移容易测量。

items.example: The redshifted lines were faint but clear.
items.exampleCN: 红移后的谱线虽淡却清楚。

items.meaning: the process of moving toward red
items.example: The redshifting of the light continued with distance.
The approaching star showed a blueshift.
items.exampleCN: 接近的恒星显示出蓝移。

items.example: Dust can redden a star's light.
Interstellar reddening is not a redshift.
A small shift in position changed the reading.
items.exampleCN: 位置的微小移动改变了读数。

definition_zh: 蓝移；光谱线整体向短波方向的移动
definition_en: the displacement of spectral lines toward shorter wavelengths, caused by motion toward the observer or by light falling into a gravitational well
core_image: 光谱图上，一条条谱线离开原位，向蓝色一端挤过去
scene: 观测者把同一颗星的两次曝光叠在一起，发现谱线这次整体向左挪到了蓝色一端。An approaching star produces a slight blueshift in its spectral lines.
sceneCN: 这里指「谱线整体向短波一端移动的现象」（第 1 个义项：波长被压缩、频率升高）；句意为正在接近的恒星使其谱线出现轻微蓝移。图中可辨识物件：两次曝光底片、谱线、比对尺、观测椅。

pos.zh: 蓝移；向短波方向的谱线位移

senses.title: Spectral lines moved toward blue
senses.titleCN: 谱线整体向短波一端移动
senses.definition: the shift of spectral lines to shorter wavelengths and higher frequencies
senses.definitionCN: 谱线向更短波长、更高频率的移动
senses.example: An approaching star produces a slight blueshift in its spectral lines.
senses.exampleCN: 正在接近的恒星使其谱线出现轻微蓝移。
senses.why: blue names the end of the visible spectrum that the lines move toward, and shift names the displacement.
senses.whyCN: blue 指谱线移向的可见光谱那一端，shift 指位移本身。

senses.title: Doppler blueshift from approach
senses.titleCN: 接近运动造成的多普勒蓝移
senses.definition: the blueshift produced when a source moves toward the observer
senses.definitionCN: 光源朝观测者运动时产生的蓝移
senses.example: The star's blueshift shows that it is falling toward us.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗星的蓝移表明它正朝我们靠近。
senses.why: an approaching source crowds the waves it sends, so the cause is motion and the effect is shorter wavelength.
senses.whyCN: 接近的光源把发出的波挤紧，因此成因是运动，结果是波长变短。

senses.title: Gravitational blueshift
senses.definition: the blueshift of light falling into a strong gravitational field
senses.definitionCN: 光落入强引力场时产生的蓝移
senses.example: Light falling toward the dense star gained a gravitational blueshift.
senses.exampleCN: 朝致密恒星下落的光获得了引力蓝移。
senses.why: light gains energy as it falls into a well, and higher energy appears at shorter wavelength.
senses.whyCN: 光落入势阱时获得能量，能量变高就表现为波长变短。

senses.title: The measured blueshift value
senses.definition: the number recording a fractional wavelength decrease, often written as a negative z
senses.definitionCN: 记录波长相对减少量的数值，常写作负的 z
senses.example: The measured blueshift was tiny, a fraction of a nanometre.
senses.exampleCN: 测得的蓝移极小，只有一纳米的一小部分。
senses.why: a value is needed for comparison, so the word also names the number, conventionally negative.
senses.whyCN: 比较需要一个数值，因此这个词也指那个数，惯例上取负值。

senses.title: A blueshifted line
senses.definition: a particular absorption or emission line found at a shorter wavelength than its laboratory position
senses.definitionCN: 出现在比实验室位置更短波长处的某条吸收线或发射线
senses.example: The blueshifted absorption line revealed hot gas moving outward.
senses.exampleCN: 蓝移的吸收线揭示出正在外流的高温气体。
senses.why: the adjective form fixes the phenomenon to individual lines, which is what observers actually measure.
senses.whyCN: 形容词形式把现象落实到一条条谱线上，而观测者测量的正是这些线。

senses.title: The counterpart of redshift
senses.definition: the opposite sign of the same displacement, used whenever sources approach or space contracts locally
senses.definitionCN: 同一位移的相反方向，用于光源接近或局部空间收缩的情形
senses.example: In the pair, one galaxy shows blueshift and the other redshift.
senses.exampleCN: 在这一对星系中，一个显示蓝移，另一个显示红移。
senses.why: redshift and blueshift name one axis in two directions, so the terms are defined against each other.
senses.whyCN: 红移与蓝移是同一条轴上的两个方向，因此这两个术语互为定义。

senses.title: Blueshift in stellar and galactic observation
senses.titleCN: 恒星与星系观测中的蓝移
senses.definition: a blueshift used to identify infalling gas, rotating companions or approaching clusters
senses.definitionCN: 用于识别内落气体、旋转伴星或接近星团的蓝移
senses.example: The blueshift of the companion star exposed the binary's orbital motion.
senses.exampleCN: 伴星的蓝移揭示了这对双星的轨道运动。
senses.why: because motion is common in binaries and clusters, blueshift became a standard diagnostic.
senses.whyCN: 由于双星与星团中运动普遍，蓝移成了标准的诊断手段。

senses.title: Figurative compression or advance
senses.definition: a borrowed use for any signal that arrives compressed, raised or early
senses.definitionCN: 借指任何到达时被压缩、被抬高或提前的信号
senses.example: The remastered track has a kind of blueshift: everything sounds tighter and higher.
senses.exampleCN: 重制后的曲目有种蓝移感：一切都更紧、更高。
senses.why: the physical crowding of waves became an image for anything that reaches us speeded up.
senses.whyCN: 波被物理挤紧，成了任何抵达时被加速的事物的意象。

intro.en: Blueshift is an English compound formed in astronomy from blue and shift. It has no Latin ancestor. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: blueshift 是英语复合词，在天文学中由 blue 与 shift 构成，没有拉丁语祖先。年代均为约数。

items.en: Blue descends from Old French bleu, itself from a Germanic source; shift goes back to Old English sciftan 'to arrange, divide'.
items.cn: blue 来自古法语 bleu，而 bleu 又出自日耳曼语来源；shift 可追溯到古英语 sciftan「安排、分配」。

items.en: The compound appeared in the twentieth century as the natural partner of redshift, once spectra were measured precisely enough.
items.cn: 这个复合词在二十世纪出现，作为红移的天然对应词，当时光谱已能被足够精确地测量。

items.en: Studies of binary stars and galaxy clusters gave the term a working role in measuring motion.
items.cn: 对双星与星系团的研究，使这个词在测量运动方面有了实际用途。

items.en: Relativity added the gravitational blueshift, extending the word beyond motion alone.
items.cn: 相对论增添了引力蓝移，把这个词扩展到运动之外。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the earliest printed use of the compound is not fixed, and the pre-Germanic origin of blue is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：这个复合词最早的印刷用例没有定论，blue 在日耳曼语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds the mirror-image terms that are routinely confused; group two holds the physical quantities involved.
note.cn: 第一组是常被混淆的镜像术语；第二组是所涉的物理量。

entries.definition: Displacement toward longer wavelengths, caused by recession, expansion or light climbing out of a well.
entries.definitionCN: 向更长波长的位移，由退行、膨胀或光爬出势阱造成。

entries.definition: The participial adjective for lines that have already moved; the noun names the phenomenon.
entries.definitionCN: 谱线已经移动的分词形容词；名词形式才指现象本身。

entries.definition: The colour itself; in the compound it only marks the direction of the shift.
entries.definitionCN: 颜色本身；在复合词中只标记位移的方向。

entries.definition: Any displacement at all; blueshift adds the spectral setting and the direction.
entries.definitionCN: 任何位移；blueshift 增添了光谱语境与方向。

entries.definition: The general frequency change from relative motion; blueshift is its short-wavelength half.
entries.definitionCN: 相对运动造成的一般频率变化；蓝移是其中短波的一半。

entries.definition: Moving nearer, the usual cause of an observed blueshift.
entries.definitionCN: 靠近的运动，是观测到蓝移的常见成因。

entries.definition: The squeezing of waves that raises frequency; blueshift is its spectral signature.
entries.definitionCN: 波被挤紧从而提高频率；蓝移是其光谱特征。

entries.definition: The distance between crests; a blueshift is a decrease in this distance.
entries.definitionCN: 波峰之间的距离；蓝移就是这一距离的缩短。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real parts, real observations and real paired terms, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实观测与真实成对术语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Blue plus shift: lines slide toward the blue end.
normal.cn: 蓝色加位移：谱线滑向蓝端。

normal.en: Approaching sources blueshift; receding sources redshift.
normal.cn: 接近的光源蓝移；远离的光源红移。

normal.en: Falling into a gravity well also produces a blueshift.
normal.cn: 落入引力势阱同样产生蓝移。

normal.en: A blueshift is a negative z on the same scale as redshift.
normal.cn: 蓝移与红移在同一标尺上取负的 z。

normal.en: Binary stars reveal their orbital motion through alternating red and blue shifts.
normal.cn: 双星通过交替的红移与蓝移显露轨道运动。

abstract.en: Picture a spring being compressed so the coils sit closer together.
abstract.cn: 想象弹簧被压紧，线圈彼此靠近。

abstract.en: Picture an ambulance growing higher in pitch as it rushes toward you.
abstract.cn: 想象救护车冲向你时音调越来越高。

abstract.en: Picture a message that arrives shorter and quicker than it was sent.
abstract.cn: 想象一条消息抵达时比发出时更短、更快。

examples.en: The blueshift of the gas cloud showed that it was falling inward.
examples.cn: 气体云的蓝移表明它正向内落。

examples.en: A negative z records a blueshift rather than a redshift.
examples.cn: 负的 z 记录的是蓝移而非红移。

examples.en: The two stars trade blueshift and redshift as they orbit.
examples.cn: 两颗星在轨道上交替呈现蓝移与红移。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「blue（蓝）+ shift（移动）」——谱线整体往蓝端移动 → 蓝移

root: 英语复合词，由 blue（经古法语 bleu，出自日耳曼语）与 shift（古英语 sciftan）构成，二十世纪在天文学中造出，无拉丁同族，拉丁条目数组留空；blue 的日耳曼语之前来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one compression: lines crowd blue, a source approaches, gravity pulls light down, a value is read, a line is identified, the term pairs with redshift, observations use it and finally any signal arrives speeded up.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一次压缩：谱线向蓝端挤、光源接近、引力把光拉下、读出数值、指认谱线、与红移成对、用于观测，最后是任何信号抵达时已被加速。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spectrum squeezed from the red end so that every line slides toward blue.
core.cn: 核心意象：光谱被从红端挤紧，每条谱线都滑向蓝端。

branches.en: ONE AXIS, TWO SIGNS: the same displacement read in the opposite direction.
branches.cn: 一条轴、两个符号：同一位移的相反方向。

branches.en: MOTION TOWARD US: approach crowds the waves and betrays orbital motion.
branches.cn: 朝我们的运动：接近把波挤紧，也泄露轨道运动。

branches.en: FALLING LIGHT: gravity, not speed, supplies the compression.
branches.cn: 下落的光：压缩来自引力，而非速度。

branches.en: VALUE AND LINE: the effect is read as a negative number on a named line.
branches.cn: 数值与谱线：效应读成负值，落在一条具名的线上。

branches.en: METAPHOR: anything that arrives tighter and higher borrows the image.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何抵达时更紧、更高的事物都借用这一意象。

intro.en: Blueshift is a two-word English compound whose halves are both ordinary words, so its meaning is fully transparent.

latinIntro.en: There are no Latin entries: blue reached English through French from a Germanic source, and shift is native Old English.

items.structure: Old French bleu, from a Germanic source
items.meaning: the colour of the clear sky
items.example: The line sits at the blue end.
The line shifted slightly.
The blueshift was easy to see.
The blueshifted line was faint.

items.meaning: the process of moving toward blue
items.example: The blueshifting of the gas continued.
The companion showed a redshift instead.
A blue filter isolates the short waves.
