items.example: The star has a bluish tint.
A small shift changed the result.
items.exampleCN: 微小的位移改变了结果。

definition_zh: 多普勒效应；波源与观测者相对运动引起接收频率变化的现象
definition_en: the change in the observed frequency of a wave caused by relative motion between the source and the observer
core_image: 一辆鸣笛的车从身边驶过，靠近时音调升高，远去时音调降低
scene: 十字路口，救护车鸣着笛驶近又远去，站在路边的人听到音调先升后降。A passing siren is a familiar example of the Doppler effect.
sceneCN: 这里指「因波源与观测者相对运动而使接收频率改变的现象」（第 1 个义项：靠近时频率升高、远离时降低）；句意为驶过鸣笛声的音调变化就是多普勒效应的常见例子。图中可辨识物件：救护车、鸣笛、路边行人、车道。

pos.zh: 多普勒效应（专有名词，通常带定冠词）

collocations.phrase: a demonstration of the Doppler effect

derivatives.zh: 多普勒的（用于雷达、超声等）

senses.title: Frequency change from relative motion
senses.titleCN: 相对运动引起的频率变化
senses.definition: the general principle that relative motion between source and observer changes the observed frequency of a wave
senses.definitionCN: 波源与观测者相对运动改变所观测到的波频率的一般原理
senses.example: A passing siren is a familiar example of the Doppler effect.
senses.exampleCN: 驶过的鸣笛声是多普勒效应的常见例子。
senses.why: Doppler names the physicist who described the principle, and effect names the phenomenon he explained.
senses.whyCN: Doppler 指描述这一原理的物理学家，effect 指他所解释的现象。

senses.title: Acoustic Doppler effect
senses.definition: the rise and fall of pitch heard when a sound source passes by
senses.definitionCN: 声源驶过时听到的音调先升后降
senses.example: The Doppler effect makes the train horn drop in pitch as it leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 多普勒效应使火车鸣笛在离去时音调下降。
senses.why: sound was the first case Doppler studied, so the acoustic use is the oldest working sense.
senses.whyCN: 声音是多普勒最早研究的情形，因此声学用法是最早的实用义项。

senses.title: Optical Doppler effect
senses.definition: the shift of spectral lines caused by the motion of a light source
senses.definitionCN: 光源运动造成的谱线位移
senses.example: The optical Doppler effect turns motion into a measurable colour shift.
senses.exampleCN: 光学多普勒效应把运动变成可测量的颜色位移。
senses.why: light obeys the same relative-motion rule as sound, but the result is read as wavelength rather than pitch.
senses.whyCN: 光遵守与声音相同的相对运动规则，只是结果读作波长而非音调。

senses.title: Doppler radar speed measurement
senses.definition: the use of reflected radio waves to measure the speed of an object
senses.definitionCN: 利用反射回来的无线电波测量物体速度
senses.example: The Doppler effect lets a radar gun read the speed of a car.
senses.exampleCN: 多普勒效应让测速雷达读出汽车的速度。
senses.why: a moving target returns a shifted echo, so the principle becomes an instrument.
senses.whyCN: 运动目标返回带位移的回波，于是原理变成了仪器。

senses.title: The frequency shift itself
senses.definition: the difference between the emitted and the received frequency
senses.definitionCN: 发出频率与接收频率之间的差
senses.example: The Doppler effect here amounts to a few kilohertz.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的多普勒效应相当于几千赫兹的频移。
senses.why: metonymy turns the principle into the amount it produces, which is what instruments record.
senses.whyCN: 借代把原理转指它所产生的那份量，而仪器记录的正是这份量。

senses.title: Medical Doppler ultrasound
senses.definition: the use of Doppler ultrasound to detect the direction and speed of blood flow
senses.definitionCN: 用多普勒超声检测血流的方向与速度
senses.example: The Doppler effect lets the scanner show blood moving through a valve.
senses.exampleCN: 多普勒效应让扫描仪显示血液流过瓣膜。
senses.why: moving blood reflects sound with a shift, so the principle became a bedside diagnostic.
senses.whyCN: 流动的血液反射声音时带有位移，于是原理成了床旁诊断手段。

senses.title: Weather Doppler radar
senses.definition: the use of Doppler radar to map the motion of rain and wind inside storms
senses.definitionCN: 用多普勒雷达绘制风暴内雨滴与风的运动
senses.example: Weather services rely on the Doppler effect to see rotation inside a storm.
senses.exampleCN: 气象部门依靠多普勒效应观察风暴内部的旋转。
senses.why: the same echo shift that measures a car also measures falling rain, scaled up to a whole storm.
senses.whyCN: 测量汽车的同一回波位移也能测量落雨，只是尺度放大到整个风暴。

senses.title: Figurative perceptual bias
senses.titleCN: 借喻：相对运动造成的感知偏差
senses.definition: a borrowed use for any distortion produced by the relative movement of observer and event
senses.definitionCN: 借指观察者与事件相对运动所造成的一切失真
senses.example: Memory has its own Doppler effect: the faster life moves, the more the past changes pitch.
senses.exampleCN: 记忆有自己的多普勒效应：生活越快，过去音调变得越多。
senses.why: the principle makes perception depend on the observer's motion, and that idea transfers readily to human experience.
senses.whyCN: 这一原理使感知取决于观察者的运动，这一观念很容易迁移到人的经验中。

intro.en: Doppler effect is an eponym: the surname Doppler plus the Latin-derived noun effect. The principle was published in 1842. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: Doppler effect 是冠名词：姓氏 Doppler 加拉丁来源的名词 effect。这一原理于 1842 年发表。年代均为约数。

items.en: Effect descends from Latin effectus, the past participle of efficere 'to bring about', built on ex- 'out' plus facere 'to do, make'.
items.cn: effect 来自拉丁 effectus，即 efficere「促成」的过去分词，由 ex-「出」加 facere「做、造」构成。

items.en: Effectus meant 'a doing, a result', and English effect kept both the sense of result and the sense of bringing something about.
items.cn: effectus 意为「做成、结果」，英语 effect 同时保留了「结果」与「促成」两层意思。

items.en: Christian Doppler, an Austrian physicist, published the principle in 1842, first for sound and then for light.
items.cn: 奥地利物理学家克里斯蒂安·多普勒于 1842 年发表这一原理，先论声音，再论光。

items.en: Experiments with moving sound sources and with starlight confirmed the effect within the following decades.
items.cn: 随后数十年间，用运动声源与星光的实验证实了这一效应。

items.en: Radar, ultrasound and astronomy turned the eponym into a family of instruments and techniques.
items.cn: 雷达、超声与天文学把这个冠名词变成了一整套仪器与技术。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the surname Doppler has a regional Germanic origin whose exact form is uncertain, and the pre-Latin origin of facere is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：姓氏 Doppler 有地区性的日耳曼语来源，确切形式不确定；facere 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds the related technical labels that are often used interchangeably; group two holds the everyday words for the same experience.
note.cn: 第一组是常被互换使用的相关技术标签；第二组是描述同一经验的日常词。

entries.definition: The frequency difference itself; the Doppler effect is the principle, and the shift is its numerical result.
entries.definitionCN: 频率差本身；多普勒效应是原理，频移是其数值结果。

entries.definition: A radar that applies the effect; the name belongs to the device, not to the physics.
entries.definitionCN: 应用这一效应的雷达；名称属于设备，而非物理原理。

entries.definition: The long-wavelength half of the optical Doppler effect, also produced by cosmic expansion.
entries.definitionCN: 光学多普勒效应的长波一半，也可由宇宙膨胀产生。

entries.definition: Any result or outcome; only the eponym fixes it to relative motion and waves.
entries.definitionCN: 任何结果或后果；只有加上冠名才限定为相对运动与波。

entries.definition: The everyday description of the acoustic case; it says nothing about the underlying wave physics.
entries.definitionCN: 对声学情形的日常描述；不涉及背后的波动原理。

entries.definition: The neutral technical name for any change in observed frequency, whatever its cause.
entries.definitionCN: 任何观测频率变化的中性技术名称，不论成因。

entries.definition: Motion of source and observer with respect to each other; it is the condition, not the effect.
entries.definitionCN: 波源与观测者相对彼此的运动；它是条件，而非效应。

entries.definition: Crests arriving closer together, which raises the observed frequency.
entries.definitionCN: 波峰来得更密，从而提高观测频率。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real physics, real instruments and real eponym usage, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的物理、真实的仪器与真实的冠名用法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Approach raises pitch; recession lowers it.
normal.cn: 靠近时音调升高；远离时音调降低。

normal.en: The effect is named after Christian Doppler, who published it in 1842.
normal.cn: 这一效应以 1842 年发表它的克里斯蒂安·多普勒命名。

normal.en: Radar guns, weather radar and medical ultrasound all run on it.
normal.cn: 测速雷达、气象雷达与医用超声都靠它工作。

normal.en: In light the effect is read as redshift or blueshift.
normal.cn: 在光中，这一效应读作红移或蓝移。

normal.en: The effect is the principle; the shift is the number.
normal.cn: 效应是原理；频移是数值。

abstract.en: Picture a runner passing a ringing bell and hearing it fall silent behind.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者经过一只响铃，听见铃声在身后低落。

abstract.en: Picture two trains passing, each hearing the other's horn change key.
abstract.cn: 想象两列火车交会，彼此听见对方的汽笛变了调。

abstract.en: Picture a memory that changes tone depending on how fast you revisit it.
abstract.cn: 想象一段记忆，因你回访的快慢而改变色调。

examples.en: The Doppler effect explains why the siren drops in pitch as the ambulance passes.
examples.cn: 多普勒效应解释了救护车驶过时警笛音调为何下降。

examples.en: Astronomers use the Doppler effect to measure the rotation of galaxies.
examples.cn: 天文学家利用多普勒效应测量星系的旋转。

examples.en: Doppler ultrasound detects the direction of blood flow through a valve.
examples.cn: 多普勒超声检测血液流过瓣膜的方向。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「Doppler（物理学家多普勒）+ effect（效应）」——他描述的运动改变音调现象 → 多普勒效应

root: 姓氏 Doppler（奥地利物理学家，1842 年发表该原理）+ 拉丁 effectus「结果」，后者来自 efficere「促成」= ex-「出」+ facere「做、造」；facere 更深来源不确定，Doppler 姓氏的日耳曼语来源形式存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one principle: relative motion changes frequency, heard as pitch, seen as colour, used by radar, measured as a shift, applied to blood, applied to storms and finally borrowed for perception.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一条原理：相对运动改变频率，听成音调、看成颜色、用于雷达、量成频移、用于血流、用于风暴，最后借用于感知。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a siren passing a listener, its pitch rising as it comes and falling as it goes.
core.cn: 核心意象：警笛经过听者，来时音调升高，去时音调降低。

branches.en: PRINCIPLE AND AMOUNT: the rule and the number it yields.
branches.cn: 原理与数值：规则本身，以及它给出的数。

branches.en: SOUND: the oldest and most familiar case.
branches.cn: 声音：最古老也最熟悉的情形。

branches.en: LIGHT AND STORMS: wavelength shifts and radar echoes share one rule.
branches.cn: 光与风暴：波长位移与雷达回波共用一条规则。

branches.en: INSTRUMENTS: speed guns and ultrasound turn the rule into a reading.
branches.cn: 仪器：测速枪与超声把规则变成读数。

branches.en: PERCEPTION: what is observed depends on how the observer moves.
branches.cn: 感知：观测到什么，取决于观测者怎样运动。

intro.en: The term joins a surname to a Latin-derived noun, so only the second half has a morphological family.
intro.cn: 这个术语把姓氏与一个拉丁来源的名词连接起来，因此只有后半有形态词族。

latinIntro.en: Effectus and efficere come from ex- plus facere; the same root builds effect, effective, efficient and factory.
latinIntro.cn: effectus 与 efficere 来自 ex- 加 facere；同一词根还构成 effect、effective、efficient 与 factory。

items.meaning: the physicist who described the principle
items.meaningCN: 描述这一原理的物理学家
items.example: Doppler published the principle in 1842.
items.exampleCN: 多普勒于 1842 年发表这一原理。

items.meaning: a result produced by a cause
items.example: The effect was easy to hear.
The Latin verb underlies the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词支撑整个词族。

items.example: The method proved effective.

items.meaning: in a way that produces a result
items.example: The two cases are effectively the same.
items.exampleCN: 这两种情形实际上是同一回事。

items.example: They tested the effectiveness of the coating.
items.exampleCN: 他们测试了涂层的有效性。

items.example: The Doppler shift was a few kilohertz.
items.exampleCN: 多普勒频移是几千赫兹。

items.example: Doppler radar tracked the storm.
items.exampleCN: 多普勒雷达追踪了风暴。

items.meaning: a place where things are made
items.example: The root facere also hides in factory.
items.exampleCN: 词根 facere 也藏在 factory 里。

definition_zh: 扩大的；膨胀的；展开的；扩展的
definition_en: growing larger in size, scope or number, or opening out from a folded or compressed state
core_image: 一只气球被不断吹大，表面的墨点彼此越离越远
scene: 吹气口接着气泵，橡胶表面上的墨点随着体积增大而彼此远离。The expanding balloon pushed its painted dots farther apart.
sceneCN: 这里指「体积不断变大的」（第 1 个义项：物体受内压或加热而向外胀大）；句意为膨胀的气球把画上的墨点推得越来越远。图中可辨识物件：气球、气泵、墨点、细绳。

pos.zh: 扩大中的；膨胀的；展开的
expand 的现在分词（正在扩大）

senses.title: Growing larger in volume
senses.definition: becoming larger in volume, as a gas, a balloon or heated metal
senses.definitionCN: 体积变大，如气体、气球或受热的金属
senses.example: The expanding balloon pushed its painted dots farther apart.
senses.exampleCN: 膨胀的气球把画上的墨点推得越来越远。
senses.why: expanding is the present participle of expand, so it names an ongoing increase rather than a finished state.
senses.whyCN: expanding 是 expand 的现在分词，因此指正在进行的增大，而非已完成的状态。

senses.title: Extending in scope
senses.definition: growing to cover more activities, customers or territory
senses.definitionCN: 扩展到覆盖更多业务、客户或地域
senses.example: The expanding company opened three new offices.
senses.exampleCN: 这家扩张中的公司新开了三处办公室。
senses.why: the physical sense of spreading outward was applied to organisations and their reach.
senses.whyCN: 向外铺展的物理义被用于组织及其覆盖面。

senses.title: Opening something folded
senses.definition: unfolding or spreading out something that was compressed
senses.definitionCN: 把被压缩或折叠的东西摊开
senses.example: The expanding map covered the whole table.
senses.exampleCN: 展开的地图铺满了整张桌子。
senses.why: the Latin root pandere meant 'to spread', and English kept that literal gesture.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 pandere 意为「铺开」，英语保留了这一具体动作。

senses.title: Developing an account in detail
senses.definition: developing a statement, story or argument at greater length
senses.definitionCN: 把陈述、故事或论证写得更长更细
senses.example: Her expanding notes turned into a full chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 她不断展开的笔记变成了一整章。
senses.why: writing that grows longer is pictured as a surface being spread out.
senses.whyCN: 越写越长的文字，被想象成一张被铺开的平面。

senses.title: The universe expanding
senses.definition: the increase of space itself, carrying galaxies apart
senses.definitionCN: 空间本身的增长，使星系彼此远离
senses.example: The expanding universe carries distant galaxies away from one another.
senses.exampleCN: 膨胀的宇宙使遥远星系彼此远离。
senses.why: cosmology reused the everyday verb for space itself, not for matter moving into empty room.
senses.whyCN: 宇宙学把这个日常动词用于空间本身，而不是物质在空房间里运动。

senses.title: Writing out a mathematical expression
senses.definition: rewriting an expression as a sum or product of simpler terms
senses.definitionCN: 把一个式子改写为更简单项的和或积
senses.example: The expanding series revealed a simple pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 展开后的级数显出一个简单规律。
senses.why: algebra speaks of expanding brackets because the written expression literally takes up more space.
senses.whyCN: 代数说「展开括号」，是因为写出来的式子确实占了更多空间。

senses.title: Increasing in number
senses.definition: growing in number, membership or quantity
senses.definitionCN: 数量、成员或总量增长
senses.example: The expanding list of members forced a larger hall.
senses.exampleCN: 不断增长的成员名单迫使换更大的礼堂。
senses.why: once scope widens, the count behind it rises, so the same participle covers numbers.
senses.whyCN: 范围一旦变宽，背后的数量就会上升，因此同一分词也覆盖数量。

senses.title: Spreading open
senses.definition: opening out something held closed, such as wings or a chest
senses.definitionCN: 把合拢的东西张开，如翅膀或胸膛
senses.example: The expanding wings caught the warm air.
senses.exampleCN: 张开的翅膀兜住暖空气。
senses.why: the oldest literal sense of spreading survives in the body and in machinery.
senses.whyCN: 「铺开」这一最古老的字面义，仍留在身体与机械的用法中。

intro.en: Expanding is the present participle of expand, from Latin expandere 'to spread out', built on ex- 'out' and pandere 'to spread'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: expanding 是 expand 的现在分词，来自拉丁 expandere「铺开」，由 ex-「向外」与 pandere「铺展」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pandere meant 'to spread out, open' and also supplied the base of the word for a spreading roof. Its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: pandere 意为「铺开、张开」，也是表示「展开的屋顶」一词的词基。其更深来源不确定。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus pandere produced expandere 'to spread out, unfold', used of hands, wings and written matter.
items.cn: ex-「向外」加 pandere 构成 expandere「铺开、展开」，用于手、翅膀与文字材料。

items.en: The verb entered English in the fifteenth century through French, first in the sense of spreading something out.
items.cn: 这个动词在十五世纪经法语进入英语，最初指把某物摊开。

items.en: From the seventeenth century gases and metals were said to expand when heated, fixing the volume sense.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，气体与金属受热时被说成 expand，从而固定了体积义。

items.en: Twentieth-century cosmology applied the participle to space itself, giving the expanding universe.
items.cn: 二十世纪的宇宙学把这个分词用于空间本身，形成了「膨胀的宇宙」。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the pre-Latin origin of pandere is not established, and any Indo-European root proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：pandere 在拉丁语之前的来源未得到证明，凡为其提出的印欧词根均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root forms that look alike; group two holds near-meaning growth words.
note.cn: 第一组是同根形近形式；第二组是语义相近的增长词。

entries.definition: The verb itself, naming the event; expanding names the event in progress or the thing undergoing it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词本身，指事件；expanding 指进行中的事件或正在经历它的东西。

entries.definition: The past participle, describing something that has already grown; expanding is still in motion.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，描述已经长大的东西；expanding 仍在进行中。

entries.definition: Describing something broad or tending to expand, often a mood or a view, not an active process.
entries.definitionCN: 描述开阔或趋于扩张的事物，多指心境或视野，而非进行中的过程。

entries.definition: The act or result of expanding; the participle points to the process, the noun to the process as a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 扩张的动作或结果；分词指向过程，名词把过程当作事物。

entries.definition: Increasing in size or number by natural development; expanding stresses outward spread.
entries.definitionCN: 经自然发育而增大或增多；expanding 强调向外铺展。

entries.definition: Becoming larger because of internal pressure or fluid; it is more physical and often unwanted.
entries.definitionCN: 因内部压力或液体而变大；更偏物理，且常含不希望的意味。

entries.definition: Increasing in width; expanding can happen in any direction or in abstract scope.
entries.definitionCN: 宽度增加；expanding 可在任何方向或抽象范围发生。

entries.definition: Becoming longer under tension; it need not add material or volume.
entries.definitionCN: 在拉力下变长；不一定增加材料或体积。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的语素与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ex- 'out' plus pandere 'spread': to spread outward.
normal.cn: ex-「向外」加 pandere「铺展」：向外铺开。

normal.en: The family runs expand, expansion, expansive, expandable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 expand、expansion、expansive、expandable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: expanding universe, expanding market, expanding foam.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：膨胀的宇宙、扩张的市场、膨胀泡沫。

normal.en: Expanding brackets in algebra literally takes up more paper.
normal.cn: 代数里展开括号，字面上确实占了更多纸面。

normal.en: The participle is active; expanded is finished.
normal.cn: 分词形式是进行中的；expanded 是已完成的。

abstract.en: Picture a balloon whose dots drift apart as it fills.
abstract.cn: 想象气球被吹大时，表面的墨点彼此漂远。

abstract.en: Picture a map unfolded until it covers the table.
abstract.cn: 想象地图被摊开，直到铺满桌面。

abstract.en: Picture a city that keeps pushing its edge outward each year.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市每年把边缘向外推。

examples.en: The expanding universe is not expanding into anything.
examples.cn: 膨胀的宇宙并不是在向某个东西里膨胀。

examples.en: The company is expanding into three new markets.
examples.cn: 这家公司正在向三个新市场扩张。

examples.en: An expanding gas does work on the piston.
examples.cn: 膨胀的气体对活塞做功。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（向外）+ pand（铺展）+ ing（进行）」——正在向外铺开 → 扩大的、膨胀的

root: 拉丁 expandere「铺开」= ex-「向外」+ pandere「铺展」；pandere 更深来源不确定，其印欧词根一说属重构。英语 expand 经法语进入，expanding 为其现在分词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one outward movement: volume swells, scope widens, a folded thing opens, an account lengthens, space itself grows, algebra spreads, numbers rise and wings open.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一次向外运动：体积胀大、范围变宽、折叠物打开、叙述变长、空间本身增长、代数式铺开、数量上升、翅膀张开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balloon filling with air, every mark on its skin moving away from every other.
core.cn: 核心意象：气球被充气，表面每个标记都离其他标记越来越远。

branches.en: VOLUME AND SPACE: from a balloon to the universe, the same outward swell.
branches.cn: 体积与空间：从气球到宇宙，同一种向外的胀大。

branches.en: SCOPE AND COUNT: wider reach brings more members and more territory.
branches.cn: 范围与数量：覆盖更广带来更多成员与更多地域。

branches.en: UNFOLDING AND OPENING: what was closed spreads open again.
branches.cn: 摊开与张开：原本合拢的重新铺开。

branches.en: DETAIL: a text occupies more space as it develops.
branches.cn: 细节：文本随展开而占据更多空间。

branches.en: ALGEBRA: symbols take up more paper when brackets are expanded.
branches.cn: 代数：展开括号后，符号占更多纸面。

intro.en: Expanding is built from the Latin verb expandere, whose prefix and root both recur in English.
intro.cn: expanding 来自拉丁动词 expandere，其前缀与词根都在英语中复现。

latinIntro.en: Ex- 'out' plus pandere 'to spread' gives expandere; the same pandere underlies expanse and the older sense of a spread roof.
latinIntro.cn: ex-「向外」加 pandere「铺展」构成 expandere；同一 pandere 还构成 expanse，以及「展开的屋顶」这一较旧义。

items.example: The prefix turns spreading into spreading outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「铺」变成「向外铺」。

items.example: Pandere is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: pandere 是整个词族的词根。

items.example: Metals expand when heated.
The expanding gas did work.

items.meaning: the act or result of expanding
items.example: The expansion of the market was rapid.
The view was expansive.
The drive is expandable.
A flat expanse of salt lay ahead.
items.exampleCN: 前方是一片平坦的盐滩。

items.example: The gas is expansible under heat.

definition_zh: 大爆炸（宇宙起源模型）；巨响；爆发式的开端
definition_en: the cosmological model in which the universe began from an extremely hot, dense state and has been expanding ever since
core_image: 一个极小的亮点在瞬间铺开，变成整片星空，时间从那一刻开始
scene: 天文馆的穹顶亮起，讲解员指向屏幕上那个由极小一点铺开的整个宇宙。The big bang model describes a universe that began from an extremely hot, dense state.
sceneCN: 这里指「描述宇宙由极热极密状态开始膨胀的模型」（第 1 个义项：宇宙起源的标准模型）；句意为大爆炸模型描述了一个从极热极密状态开始的宇宙。图中可辨识物件：穹顶屏、光点、星系投影、讲解员的手。

pos.zh: 大爆炸（宇宙起源模型或该事件）；巨响

collocations.phrase: the moment of the big bang

derivatives.zh: 爆竹；破旧汽车（英式口语）

senses.title: The standard cosmological model
senses.definition: the model in which the universe expanded from an extremely hot, dense early state
senses.definitionCN: 认为宇宙由极热极密的早期状态膨胀而来的模型
senses.example: The big bang model describes a universe that began from an extremely hot, dense state.
senses.exampleCN: 大爆炸模型描述了一个从极热极密状态开始的宇宙。
senses.why: big and bang name a large sudden event, and the phrase was fixed as the label of the leading cosmological model.
senses.whyCN: big 与 bang 指一次巨大而突然的事件，这个短语被固定为主导宇宙学模型的名称。

senses.title: The initial event itself
senses.definition: the hot, dense beginning from which the expansion is said to have started
senses.definitionCN: 据称膨胀由之开始的那个极热极密的开端
senses.example: Nothing in the model places the big bang at a particular point in space.
senses.exampleCN: 模型并没有把大爆炸放在空间中的某个特定点。
senses.why: the name of the model was transferred to the event the model describes, a common metonymy.
senses.whyCN: 模型的名称被转移到模型所描述的事件上，这是常见的借代。

senses.title: The theory as a named body of work
senses.titleCN: 作为成套理论的大爆炸学说
senses.definition: the body of theory, evidence and calculation that goes by this name
senses.definitionCN: 以这个名称统称的理论、证据与计算总体
senses.example: The big bang gained acceptance only after the relic radiation was found.
senses.exampleCN: 直到发现遗留辐射之后，大爆炸学说才被接受。
senses.why: a short label is convenient for a whole research programme, so the phrase also names the theory.
senses.whyCN: 一个简短标签便于指称整套研究纲领，因此这个短语也指理论本身。

senses.title: Relic radiation as evidence
senses.definition: the cooled afterglow of the early universe, used as the main evidence for the model
senses.definitionCN: 早期宇宙冷却后的余晖，是该模型的主要证据
senses.example: The faint glow everywhere in the sky is the big bang seen from every direction.
senses.exampleCN: 天空中无处不在的微光，就是从各个方向看到的大爆炸。
senses.why: because the afterglow fills all space, the phrase can stand for the observable trace of the event.
senses.whyCN: 由于余晖充满整个空间，这个短语可以指该事件的可观测痕迹。

senses.title: Nucleosynthesis in the early universe
senses.definition: the formation of the first light nuclei in the first minutes of expansion
senses.definitionCN: 膨胀最初几分钟内轻核的形成
senses.example: Big bang nucleosynthesis fixed the first ratio of hydrogen to helium.
senses.exampleCN: 大爆炸核合成固定了最初的氢氦比例。
senses.why: the phrase is used as a time marker for the earliest chemical events.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语被当作最早化学事件的时间标记。

senses.title: Figurative sudden fresh start
senses.definition: a borrowed use for a project or period that starts abruptly and completely
senses.definitionCN: 借指骤然且彻底开始的项目或时期
senses.example: The reform was a big bang that replaced every rule at once.
senses.exampleCN: 这次改革是一次大爆炸，一次换掉所有规则。
senses.why: the cosmic image of everything beginning at once suits any wholesale break with the past.
senses.whyCN: 万物同时开始的宇宙意象，很适合任何与过去的彻底断裂。

senses.title: A literal loud explosion
senses.definition: a very loud bang, especially a violent burst or explosion
senses.definitionCN: 一声很响的爆响，尤指猛烈的爆裂或爆炸
senses.example: The firework ended with a big bang that shook the windows.
senses.exampleCN: 烟花以一声震窗的巨响收尾。
senses.why: the two ordinary words keep their literal force, so the phrase can describe any loud blast.
senses.whyCN: 两个普通词保留了字面力量，因此这个短语可以描述任何巨响。

senses.title: Grand public launch
senses.definition: a marketing or public idiom for launching something with maximum noise and attention
senses.definitionCN: 以最大声势与关注度推出某物的市场或公众用语
senses.example: The product went out with a big bang and sold out in a day.
senses.exampleCN: 这款产品声势浩大地推出，一天就卖光了。
senses.why: the literal noise became a metaphor for publicity, and the idiom now belongs to business speech.
senses.whyCN: 字面上的响声成了宣传的比喻，这个成语如今属于商业语言。

intro.en: Big bang is an English phrase made of two ordinary words and adopted as a term in 1949. It has no Latin ancestor. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: big bang 是由两个普通英语词构成的短语，于 1949 年被采用为术语，没有拉丁语祖先。年代均为约数。

items.en: Big descends from Middle English, and bang is probably imitative of a heavy blow; the origin of bang is not settled.
items.cn: big 可追溯到中古英语；bang 很可能是对沉重撞击的拟声词，其来源没有定论。

items.en: The astronomer Fred Hoyle used the phrase on radio in 1949, apparently to mock the rival model rather than to name it respectfully.
items.cn: 天文学家弗雷德·霍伊尔于 1949 年在广播中使用这个短语，显然是为了嘲弄对立的模型，而非恭敬地命名。

items.en: Supporters of the model took the catchy phrase for their own, and it became the standard label within a decade.
items.cn: 该模型的支持者把这个顺口的说法据为己用，十年内它成了标准名称。

items.en: After the discovery of the relic radiation in the 1960s, the phrase spread from specialists to textbooks and newspapers.
items.cn: 二十世纪六十年代发现遗留辐射之后，这个短语从专家圈扩散到教科书与报纸。

items.en: The older literal sense of a loud blast survived alongside the technical one, and business speech added a third figurative use.
items.cn: 「巨响」这一较早的字面义与技术义并存，商业语言又添了第三种比喻用法。

items.en: Source uncertain (parts and first date): bang is probably imitative, which means no deeper etymology can be demonstrated, and the exact first broadcast wording is not fully documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定（成分与首见年代）：bang 很可能是拟声词，因此无法证明更深的词源；首次广播的确切措辞也没有完整记录。

note.en: Group one holds the cosmological labels that are easily swapped; group two holds ordinary words for a sudden loud event.
note.cn: 第一组是易被互换的宇宙学标签；第二组是表示骤然巨响的普通词。

entries.definition: The full name of the theoretical framework; the shorter phrase can mean the model, the event or the literal blast.
entries.definitionCN: 理论框架的完整名称；较短的说法可指模型、事件或字面巨响。

entries.definition: The competing model in which the universe looks the same at all times and new matter appears as it expands.
entries.definitionCN: 竞争模型，认为宇宙在任何时刻看起来都一样，膨胀时不断有新物质出现。

entries.definition: The point where the equations break down; it is a mathematical limit, not a synonym for the big bang.
entries.definitionCN: 方程失效之处；是数学极限，并非大爆炸的同义词。

entries.definition: A loud knock or explosion; only the phrase fixes it to the cosmological model.
entries.definitionCN: 响亮的敲击或爆炸声；只有整个短语才把它限定为宇宙学模型。

entries.definition: A violent release of energy in space; the cosmological event was not an explosion in this sense.
entries.definitionCN: 空间中能量的猛烈释放；宇宙学事件并非此义的爆炸。

entries.definition: The growth of space over time; it is what the model predicts, not the beginning itself.
entries.definitionCN: 空间随时间的增长；这是模型预言的，而非开端本身。

entries.definition: The starting point of anything; it is neutral, while big bang names a specific model.
entries.definitionCN: 任何事物的起点；它是中性的，而大爆炸指一个特定模型。

entries.definition: A formal or literary word for a beginning, often with a sense of creation.
entries.definitionCN: 正式或文学性的「开端」，常带创造意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real physics history and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的物理学史与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The name was coined in 1949 by Fred Hoyle, who did not support the model.
normal.cn: 这个名字由不支持该模型的弗雷德·霍伊尔于 1949 年造出。

normal.en: It was not an explosion in space; space itself expanded.
normal.cn: 它不是空间中的爆炸；膨胀的是空间本身。

normal.en: The relic radiation is the afterglow of the early hot state.
normal.cn: 遗留辐射是早期热状态的余晖。

normal.en: Big bang nucleosynthesis set the first hydrogen and helium ratio.
normal.cn: 大爆炸核合成定下最初的氢氦比例。

normal.en: The literal sense survives in fireworks and in the idiom with a big bang.
normal.cn: 字面义仍留在烟花与「声势浩大」的说法里。

abstract.en: Picture a single point that contains everything and then is everywhere.
abstract.cn: 想象一个包含一切的点，随后散布到处处。

abstract.en: Picture a bell struck once at the beginning of time, still ringing.
abstract.cn: 想象时间之初敲响的一只钟，至今仍在响。

abstract.en: Picture a project that replaces every old rule on its first day.
abstract.cn: 想象一个项目在第一天就换掉所有旧规则。

examples.en: The big bang model does not claim that there was an explosion at a centre.
examples.cn: 大爆炸模型并不主张在某个中心发生过爆炸。

examples.en: Big bang nucleosynthesis explains the abundance of light elements.
examples.cn: 大爆炸核合成解释了轻元素的丰度。

examples.en: The campaign began with a big bang and then went quiet.
examples.cn: 这场宣传活动声势浩大地开始，随后归于沉寂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「big（大）+ bang（巨响）」——一次巨大爆响般的开端，被借作宇宙起源模型的名称 → 大爆炸

root: 英语短语，big 可追溯到中古英语，bang 很可能是拟声词，来源不确定；1949 年由霍伊尔在广播中用作术语。无拉丁同族，拉丁条目数组留空。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one label: it names a model, the event, the theory, its afterglow, its first chemistry, a sudden new start, a literal blast and a loud launch.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个标签：它命名一个模型、一次事件、一套理论、那片余晖、最初化学、骤然新开端、字面巨响与声势浩大的推出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single brilliant point opening into a whole sky, with time starting at that instant.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个极亮的点铺开成整片天空，时间从那一刻开始。

branches.en: MODEL AND THEORY: one name covers both the idea and the programme built on it.
branches.cn: 模型与理论：同一个名称既指观念，也指建立在它之上的研究纲领。

branches.en: EVENT AND TRACE: the beginning itself and the afterglow by which it is known.
branches.cn: 事件与痕迹：开端本身，以及据以认识它的余晖。

branches.en: FIRST CHEMISTRY: the earliest minutes produced the first nuclei.
branches.cn: 最初的化学：最早几分钟造出第一批原子核。

branches.en: SUDDEN START: any wholesale new beginning borrows the image.
branches.cn: 骤然开端：任何彻底的新开始都借用这一意象。

branches.en: LITERAL NOISE: a real blast and a noisy public launch.
branches.cn: 字面响声：真实的爆炸与声势浩大的公开推出。

intro.en: Big bang is a phrase of two plain English words, so it has no morphological family beyond the words it contains.
intro.cn: big bang 是由两个普通英语词构成的短语，除所含的词以外没有额外的形态词族。

latinIntro.en: There are no Latin entries: both words are English, and the phrase was coined in twentieth-century astronomy.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁条目：两个词都是英语词，这个短语在二十世纪天文学中造出。

items.example: A big change followed.
The door shut with a bang.

items.meaning: the cosmological model or a great blast
items.example: The big bang model is well tested.
items.exampleCN: 大爆炸模型经受了充分检验。

items.example: The children lit a banger.
The banging woke the street.
He banged the drum.

items.meaning: the full name of the framework
items.meaningCN: 大爆炸理论的完整名称
items.example: The Big Bang theory rests on several lines of evidence.
items.exampleCN: 大爆炸理论建立在多条证据之上。

items.structure: big bang used as a modifier
items.example: They chose a big-bang reform.
items.exampleCN: 他们选择了骤然彻底的改革。

definition_zh: 宇宙学；宇宙的总体模型；宇宙观
definition_en: the study of the universe as a whole, its structure, origin and evolution, or a particular account of it
core_image: 一整面墙的星系分布图上，星系沿纤维状结构排成网
scene: 研究室内，一张覆盖整面墙的星系分布图前，研究员用尺子量出结构的尺度。Modern cosmology rests on the assumption that the universe looks the same on very large scales.
sceneCN: 这里指「研究宇宙整体结构、起源与演化的学科」（第 1 个义项：把宇宙当作一个整体来研究）；句意为现代宇宙学建立在宇宙在极大尺度上各处相同的假设之上。图中可辨识物件：星系分布图、长尺、研究台、墙面。

pos.zh: 宇宙学；（某一套）宇宙模型或宇宙观

senses.title: The study of the universe as a whole
senses.titleCN: 把宇宙作为整体来研究的学科
senses.definition: the branch of science that studies the structure, origin and evolution of the universe as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 把宇宙整体作为对象，研究其结构、起源与演化的科学分支
senses.example: Modern cosmology rests on the assumption that the universe looks the same on very large scales.
senses.exampleCN: 现代宇宙学建立在宇宙在极大尺度上各处相同的假设之上。
senses.why: kosmos named an ordered whole and -logia named its study, so the word literally means the account of the ordered whole.
senses.whyCN: kosmos 指有序的整体，-logia 指对它的研究，因此这个词字面上就是「关于有序整体的论述」。

senses.title: A particular model of the universe
senses.titleCN: 某一套具体的宇宙模型
senses.definition: a specific description of how the universe is arranged and how it behaves
senses.definitionCN: 对宇宙如何构成、如何运作的具体描述
senses.example: The two cosmologies disagree about how the expansion began.
senses.exampleCN: 这两套宇宙模型对膨胀如何开始意见不一。
senses.why: a field of study is often named by its product, so cosmology also means one model within the field.
senses.whyCN: 学科常以其产物命名，因此 cosmology 也指该领域内的一套模型。

senses.title: A cultural or ancient world view
senses.titleCN: 文化性或古代的宇宙观
senses.definition: a traditional or philosophical account of the world's order, not a scientific model
senses.definitionCN: 关于世界秩序的传统或哲学叙述，而非科学模型
senses.example: The cosmology of the poem places the earth at the centre of a layered sky.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗的宇宙观把大地放在层叠天空的中心。
senses.why: before the scientific sense existed, cosmologies were told as stories about order, and that older use survives.
senses.whyCN: 在科学义出现之前，宇宙观是以故事讲述秩序，这一较旧的用法仍存。

senses.title: Physical cosmology
senses.definition: the branch that applies physics to the universe, including its expansion and contents
senses.definitionCN: 把物理学用于宇宙的分支，包括其膨胀与内容物
senses.example: Physical cosmology treats the whole universe as a laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 物理宇宙学把整个宇宙当作实验室。
senses.why: the adjective marks the method: physical laws applied on the largest scale.
senses.whyCN: 形容词标记方法：在最大尺度上应用物理定律。

senses.title: Observational cosmology
senses.definition: the branch that tests models against telescope data
senses.definitionCN: 用望远镜数据检验模型的分支
senses.example: Observational cosmology measures distant supernovae to test the expansion history.
senses.exampleCN: 观测宇宙学测量遥远超新星，以检验膨胀史。
senses.why: the adjective marks the evidence side, as opposed to the theoretical side.
senses.whyCN: 形容词标记证据一侧，与理论一侧相对。

senses.title: The subject as a field of study
senses.titleCN: 作为学科领域或课程的宇宙学
senses.definition: the academic subject, course or department bearing this name
senses.definitionCN: 以此命名的学术科目、课程或系别
senses.example: She teaches cosmology in the physics department.
senses.exampleCN: 她在物理系教授宇宙学。
senses.why: a discipline's name doubles as the name of its teaching and its community.
senses.whyCN: 学科名称也用作其教学与学术社群的名称。

senses.title: The large-scale structure picture
senses.definition: the overall arrangement of galaxies and voids revealed by surveys
senses.definitionCN: 巡天揭示的星系与空洞的整体排布
senses.example: The new cosmology of the survey shows a web of filaments and voids.
senses.exampleCN: 这次巡天呈现的新宇宙图景显示出纤维与空洞组成的网。
senses.why: the word can name the picture produced by observation rather than the discipline itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以指观测产生的图景，而非学科本身。

senses.title: Figurative grand world view
senses.definition: a borrowed use for a person's or a movement's grand view of how things fit together
senses.definitionCN: 借指个人或运动对事物如何拼合的整体看法
senses.example: His cosmology of the company left no room for small experiments.
senses.exampleCN: 他的公司宇宙观不给小规模试验留空间。
senses.why: if cosmology is an account of the whole, any all-embracing world view can borrow the word.
senses.whyCN: 既然宇宙学是关于整体的叙述，任何包罗万象的世界观都能借用这个词。

intro.en: Cosmology joins Greek kosmos 'order, world' to -logia 'study, discourse'. The Latinized form cosmologia is early modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cosmology 把希腊 kosmos「秩序、世界」与 -logia「研究、论述」连接起来；拉丁化形式 cosmologia 出现在近代早期。年代均为约数。

items.en: Kosmos meant 'order, arrangement, ornament' and later 'the ordered world'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the link to a root meaning 'to arrange' is a hypothesis.
items.cn: kosmos 意为「秩序、排列、装饰」，后指「有序的世界」。其更深来源不确定；与意为「安排」的词根的联系只是假说。

items.en: -Logia meant 'speaking, account, study' and became the productive suffix of learned subjects.
items.cn: -logia 意为「讲述、论述、研究」，后来成为学术科目能产的后缀。

items.en: Early modern Latin coined cosmologia after Greek models, and the word reached English in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 近代早期拉丁语仿希腊模式造出 cosmologia，这个词在十七世纪进入英语。

items.en: In the twentieth century cosmology became an observational and physical science rather than a speculative account.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，宇宙学成为观测与物理的科学，而不再是思辨叙述。

items.en: The phrase standard model of cosmology now names the framework built on general relativity plus dark components.
items.cn: 「宇宙学标准模型」如今指建立在广义相对论加暗成分之上的框架。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the pre-Greek source of kosmos is unknown, and the etymology sometimes offered from a verb of arranging is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：kosmos 在希腊语之前的来源不明，常被提出的「源自表示安排的动词」一说属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the look-alike discipline names that are often confused; group two holds words for a whole-world account.
note.cn: 第一组是易混淆的形近学科名；第二组是表示整体世界叙述的词。

entries.definition: The study or story of how the universe came into being; cosmology covers the whole history, not only the birth.
entries.definitionCN: 研究或叙述宇宙如何诞生；宇宙学覆盖整段历史，而不只是诞生。

entries.definition: The descriptive mapping of the known universe; it does not build physical models.
entries.definitionCN: 对已知宇宙的描述性测绘；不建立物理模型。

entries.definition: The study of all celestial objects; cosmology is the part concerned with the universe as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 研究一切天体的学科；宇宙学是其中关心宇宙整体的部分。

entries.definition: The ordered universe itself; cosmology is the account of it.
entries.definitionCN: 有序的宇宙本身；宇宙学是关于它的论述。

entries.definition: A person's or culture's overall way of seeing reality; it need not be scientific or systematic.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或文化看待现实的整体方式；不必科学或系统。

entries.definition: All existing space and matter; cosmology is the study of this whole.
entries.definitionCN: 存在的一切空间与物质；宇宙学是研究这个整体。

entries.definition: The physics of individual stars and galaxies; cosmology applies physics to the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 研究单个恒星与星系的物理；宇宙学把物理用于整体。

entries.definition: Philosophical inquiry into being and reality; it can overlap with cosmology but is not observational.
entries.definitionCN: 对存在与现实的哲学探究；可与宇宙学重叠，但不是观测性的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek morphemes and real discipline names, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊语素与真实学科名，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: kosmos 'ordered world' plus -logia 'study' gives the study of the whole.
normal.cn: kosmos「有序世界」加 -logia「研究」即对整体的研究。

normal.en: Cosmology studies the whole; cosmogony studies only the birth.
normal.cn: 宇宙学研究整体；宇宙起源论只研究诞生。

normal.en: Astronomy is the wider field; cosmology is its whole-universe branch.
normal.cn: 天文学是更宽的领域；宇宙学是其整体宇宙分支。

normal.en: Physical and observational mark the two sides of the same subject.
normal.cn: 物理与观测标记同一学科的两个侧面。

normal.en: The standard model of cosmology is the current working framework.
normal.cn: 宇宙学标准模型是当前的工作框架。

abstract.en: Picture a wall-sized map where galaxies form a web of threads.
abstract.cn: 想象一面墙大的图，星系组成丝网。

abstract.en: Picture an ancient sky chart drawn as a story about order.
abstract.cn: 想象一张古代星图，被画成关于秩序的故事。

abstract.en: Picture someone who sees a company as a whole cosmos with its own laws.
abstract.cn: 想象有人把一家公司看成一个有自身定律的完整宇宙。

examples.en: Cosmology has moved from speculation to precision measurement.
examples.cn: 宇宙学已从思辨走向精密测量。

examples.en: The course covers cosmology, galaxies and stellar structure.
examples.cn: 这门课程涵盖宇宙学、星系与恒星结构。

examples.en: Her cosmology of history gives every century a fixed role.
examples.cn: 她的历史宇宙观给每个世纪安排了固定角色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「cosmos（有序世界）+ logy（研究）」——研究作为整体的宇宙 → 宇宙学

root: 希腊 kosmos「秩序、有序世界」+ -logia「研究、论述」，拉丁化形式 cosmologia；kosmos 更深来源不确定，其与「安排」词根的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one account of the whole: the discipline, a model, a cultural story, its physical side, its observational side, its teaching, the picture it produces and finally any grand outlook.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一份整体叙述：学科、模型、文化故事、物理一面、观测一面、教学、所产生的图景，最后是任何宏观世界观。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall-sized map of galaxies whose threads and voids are read as one ordered whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整面墙的星系图，丝线与空洞被读成一个有序整体。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE: the subject itself, defined by the whole it studies.
branches.cn: 学科：以它所研究的整体来界定的学科本身。

branches.en: MODEL AND PHYSICS: a specific account tested with physical laws.
branches.cn: 模型与物理：用物理定律检验的具体叙述。

branches.en: CULTURE: an older story of order that survives beside the science.
branches.cn: 文化：与科学并存的一种较旧的秩序故事。

branches.en: OBSERVATION: the data side and the picture the data yields.
branches.cn: 观测：数据一面，以及数据给出的图景。

branches.en: TEACHING AND OUTLOOK: the subject as a course, and any all-embracing view.
branches.cn: 教学与世界观：作为课程的学科，以及任何包罗万象的看法。

intro.en: Cosmology is a Greek compound of a noun and a productive suffix, both of which recur across English.
intro.cn: cosmology 是由希腊名词与能产后缀构成的复合词，两部分都在英语中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latinized Greek supplies cosmologia and cosmos; the Latin layer also gives universum, a native rival for 'the whole'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁化的希腊语提供 cosmologia 与 cosmos；拉丁层还给出 universum，作为「整体」的本族竞争者。

items.example: Kosmos is the first half of the word.
The suffix names a learned subject.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名一门学问。

items.meaning: the study of the universe as a whole
items.meaningCN: 把宇宙作为整体来研究
items.example: Cosmology asks how the whole began.
items.exampleCN: 宇宙学追问整体如何开始。

items.example: The cosmological model was revised.
The cosmologist measured the expansion rate.
items.exampleCN: 宇宙学家测量了膨胀速率。

items.example: The cosmos is not the same word as the study.
items.exampleCN: cosmos 与表示研究的词并不是同一个词。

items.meaning: the account of the universe's birth
items.example: Cosmogony covers only the beginning.
items.exampleCN: 宇宙起源论只覆盖开端。

items.meaning: a small world seen as a whole
items.example: The pond was a microcosm of the valley.
items.exampleCN: 这个池塘是山谷的缩影。

items.example: Cosmography maps without modelling.

definition_zh: 宇宙学的；与宇宙整体尺度及其演化有关的
definition_en: relating to cosmology or to the universe considered on its largest scales
core_image: 一把量到星系际距离的尺子，刻度以亿光年为单位
scene: 天文学课堂上，教师在黑板上画出随距离增大的红移曲线，标出对应的距离刻度。The cosmological redshift is treated as a stretching of space rather than motion through it.
sceneCN: 这里指「与宇宙整体尺度及其演化有关的」（第 1 个义项：属于宇宙学范围的）；句意为宇宙学红移被理解为空间的拉伸，而不是在空间中的运动。图中可辨识物件：黑板曲线、坐标轴、红移标记、粉笔。

pos.zh: 宇宙学的；宇宙整体尺度的

senses.title: Relating to cosmology
senses.definition: belonging to or studied within cosmology
senses.definitionCN: 属于宇宙学或在宇宙学范围内研究的
senses.example: The paper sits at the cosmological end of astrophysics.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文位于天体物理学的宇宙学一端。
senses.why: -ical turns the noun cosmology into the adjective of relation, so the word simply means 'of cosmology'.
senses.whyCN: -ical 把名词 cosmology 变成表关系的形容词，因此这个词就是「宇宙学的」。

senses.title: Cosmological redshift
senses.definition: the redshift produced by the expansion of space during the light's journey
senses.definitionCN: 光在旅途中因空间膨胀而产生的红移
senses.example: The cosmological redshift is treated as a stretching of space rather than motion through it.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙学红移被理解为空间的拉伸，而不是在空间中的运动。
senses.why: the adjective marks the cause: expansion of the whole, not local motion of a source.
senses.whyCN: 形容词标记成因：整体空间的膨胀，而非光源的局部运动。

senses.title: Cosmological distance
senses.definition: a distance defined with the expansion of the universe taken into account
senses.definitionCN: 把宇宙膨胀计入其中而定义的距离
senses.example: Cosmological distance is not a single number but a family of measures.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙学距离不是一个单一数值，而是一组测量。
senses.why: expanding space makes ordinary distance ambiguous, so the adjective marks a distance defined on the cosmic model.
senses.whyCN: 空间膨胀使普通距离含混，因此形容词标记一种在宇宙模型上定义的距离。

senses.title: Cosmological constant
senses.definition: the constant term Einstein added to his equations, now identified with dark energy
senses.definitionCN: 爱因斯坦加入方程的那个常数项，如今与暗能量相联系
senses.example: The cosmological constant is measured to be very small but not zero.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙学常数被测得极小，但不为零。
senses.why: the adjective fixes the constant as one belonging to the equations of the whole universe.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把这个常数限定为属于整个宇宙方程的那一个。

senses.title: Cosmological model
senses.definition: a mathematical description of the universe's geometry and history
senses.definitionCN: 对宇宙几何与历史的数学描述
senses.example: Each cosmological model predicts a different expansion history.
senses.exampleCN: 每个宇宙学模型都预言不同的膨胀史。
senses.why: the adjective distinguishes models of the whole from models of a single object.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把整体模型与单个天体的模型区分开。

senses.title: Cosmological time scale
senses.definition: a span of time comparable with the age of the universe
senses.definitionCN: 可与宇宙年龄相比的时间跨度
senses.example: On a cosmological time scale, a century is invisible.
senses.exampleCN: 在宇宙学时间尺度上，一个世纪根本看不见。
senses.why: the adjective rescales time to the whole history rather than to human experience.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把时间重新标度到整段历史，而非人类经验。

senses.title: Cosmological principle
senses.definition: the assumption that on large scales the universe is homogeneous and isotropic
senses.definitionCN: 假设宇宙在极大尺度上是均匀且各向同性的
senses.example: The cosmological principle lets one model describe the whole sky.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙学原理使一个模型足以描述整片天空。
senses.why: a principle about the whole deserves the adjective, since it is assumed before any local measurement.
senses.whyCN: 关于整体的原理理应用这个形容词，因为它在任何局部测量之前就被假设。

senses.title: Figurative vast in scale
senses.definition: a borrowed use for anything measured on an enormous scale
senses.definitionCN: 借指任何以极大尺度衡量的事物
senses.example: The company's failure was cosmological in its own small universe.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司的失败在它自己的小宇宙里是宇宙级的。
senses.why: the largest available scale became an intensifier for scale itself.
senses.whyCN: 可用的最大尺度成了「尺度」本身的加强语。

intro.en: Cosmological is cosmology plus the relational suffix -ical, from Greek kosmos and -logia through Latinized forms. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cosmological 是 cosmology 加表关系的后缀 -ical，源于希腊 kosmos 与 -logia 的拉丁化形式。年代均为约数。

items.en: Kosmos meant 'order' and then 'the ordered world'; its deeper origin is unsettled.
items.cn: kosmos 意为「秩序」，后指「有序的世界」；其更深来源无定论。

items.en: -Logia 'account, study' produced cosmology through Latinized cosmologia in the early modern period.
items.cn: -logia「论述、研究」在近代早期经拉丁化 cosmologia 产生 cosmology。

items.en: The relational suffix -ical came through Latin -icalis and French -ique, and turns the noun into an adjective of belonging.
items.cn: 表关系的后缀 -ical 经拉丁 -icalis 与法语 -ique 而来，把名词变成表归属的形容词。

items.en: The cosmological constant entered physics with Einstein's 1917 paper on the universe as a whole.
items.cn: 宇宙学常数随爱因斯坦 1917 年关于整体宇宙的论文进入物理学。

items.en: Twentieth-century cosmology multiplied fixed phrases such as cosmological redshift, distance and principle.
items.cn: 二十世纪的宇宙学衍生出宇宙学红移、宇宙学距离、宇宙学原理等大量固定短语。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the pre-Greek source of kosmos is unknown, and the root sometimes proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：kosmos 在希腊语之前的来源不明，常为其提出的词根属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the look-alike adjectives built on the same stem; group two holds near-meaning scale words.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干构成的形近形容词；第二组是语义相近的尺度词。

entries.definition: A specific term in the equations; the adjective alone does not name that term.
entries.definitionCN: 方程中的特定术语；单用形容词并不指这个术语。

entries.definition: Formed by cosmic rays in the atmosphere or in rock, a different compound with -genic.
entries.definitionCN: 由宇宙射线在大气或岩石中生成的，是带 -genic 的另一个复合词。

entries.tag: of space, not of the study
entries.definition: Belonging to outer space generally; cosmological specifically refers to the universe as a modelled whole.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指属于外层空间的；cosmological 特指作为被建模整体的宇宙。

entries.definition: Built on kosmos plus polites 'citizen': worldly and international, not cosmological at all.
entries.definitionCN: 由 kosmos 加 polites「公民」构成：世界性的、国际的，与宇宙学无关。

entries.definition: Applying to everything without exception; cosmological describes the universe as an object of study.
entries.definitionCN: 无例外地适用于一切；cosmological 描述作为研究对象的宇宙。

entries.definition: Relating to the physics of stars and galaxies rather than the whole universe.
entries.definitionCN: 与恒星和星系的物理有关，而非整个宇宙。

entries.definition: Relating to planets; it marks a much smaller scale than the cosmological one.
entries.definitionCN: 与行星有关；其尺度远小于宇宙学尺度。

entries.definition: Covering a whole system or planet; it is a general word for totality, not a cosmic term.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖整个系统或行星；是表示整体的普通词，并非宇宙术语。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的后缀与真实固定短语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Cosmology plus -ical makes the adjective of relation.
normal.cn: cosmology 加 -ical 构成表关系的形容词。

normal.en: The cosmological principle assumes the same physics everywhere on large scales.
normal.cn: 宇宙学原理假设极大尺度上处处物理相同。

normal.en: Cosmological redshift comes from stretched space, not from local motion.
normal.cn: 宇宙学红移来自被拉伸的空间，而非局部运动。

normal.en: The cosmological constant is now tied to dark energy.
normal.cn: 宇宙学常数如今与暗能量相联系。

normal.en: Cosmic means space in general; cosmological means the modelled whole.
normal.cn: cosmic 泛指太空；cosmological 指被建模的整体。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler whose marks are counted in billions of light years.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺，刻度以十亿光年计。

abstract.en: Picture a curve on a blackboard that rises with distance.
abstract.cn: 想象黑板上一条随距离上升的曲线。

abstract.en: Picture a failure so large that it fills a small private universe.
abstract.cn: 想象一次大到填满私人小宇宙的失败。

examples.en: Cosmological measurements now constrain the age of the universe.
examples.cn: 宇宙学测量如今约束着宇宙年龄。

examples.en: The cosmological constant remains one of physics' deepest puzzles.
examples.cn: 宇宙学常数仍是物理学最深的谜题之一。

examples.en: On a cosmological scale, the whole human record is a brief flicker.
examples.cn: 在宇宙尺度上，整个人类记录只是一闪。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one relational adjective: it marks the discipline, then redshift, distance, a constant, a model, a time scale, a principle and finally any enormous scale.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个关系形容词：它标记学科，继而标记红移、距离、常数、模型、时间尺度、原理，最后是任何巨大尺度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler graduated in billions of light years laid across a blackboard curve.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把以十亿光年为刻度的尺，横放在黑板上的曲线旁。

branches.en: RELATION AND INTENSITY: from 'of cosmology' to 'vast beyond measure'.
branches.cn: 关系与强度：从「属于宇宙学」到「大到无法量」。

branches.en: REDSHIFT: the adjective marks expansion as the cause.
branches.cn: 红移：形容词标记膨胀为成因。

branches.en: DISTANCE AND TIME: both are rescaled to the whole history.
branches.cn: 距离与时间：两者都被重新标度到整段历史。

branches.en: CONSTANT: a term fixed inside the equations of the whole.
branches.cn: 常数：固定在整体方程里的一个项。

branches.en: MODEL AND PRINCIPLE: the framework and the assumption beneath it.
branches.cn: 模型与原理：框架，以及它底下的假设。

intro.en: Cosmological is a derived adjective: a Greek compound noun plus a Latin-French relational suffix.
