definition_zh: 起源；起点；出身；来源；原点
definition_en: the point at which something begins, the source from which it comes, or the fixed point of a coordinate system
core_image: 一条河从山间石缝里冒出第一股水，往下越流越宽
scene: 山谷尽头，向导蹲下身，指着石缝里冒出的第一股水，说明这条河从这里开始。The origin of the river lies in a spring high in the mountains.
sceneCN: 这里指「事物开始出现的地点或起点」（第 1 个义项：时间与空间上的开端）；句意为这条河的源头在高山中的一处泉水。图中可辨识物件：石缝、泉水、山谷、向导的手。

pos.zh: 起源；起点；出身；来源；原点

senses.title: The point where something begins
senses.definition: the place or moment at which something first exists or starts
senses.definitionCN: 某物首次存在或开始的地点或时刻
senses.example: The origin of the river lies in a spring high in the mountains.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河的源头在高山中的一处泉水。
senses.why: origo in Latin meant 'a beginning, a rising', from oriri 'to rise', so the word pictures something rising into existence.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 origo 意为「开端、升起」，来自 oriri「升起」，因此这个词把事物想象为升起来而存在。

senses.title: Ancestry and social background
senses.definition: a person's family background or the place a family comes from
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的家庭背景或家族来处
senses.example: Her origin was a small farming village in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 她的出身是北方一个小农村。
senses.why: a family's beginning is its first known place, so the word moved from places to people.
senses.whyCN: 家族的起点就是它最早可考的地方，于是这个词从地点移到了人身上。

senses.title: Source or provenance of a thing
senses.definition: the place or process a product or material comes from
senses.definitionCN: 产品或材料所来自的地方或过程
senses.example: The label records the origin of every bean in the bag.
senses.exampleCN: 标签记录袋中每颗豆子的原产地。
senses.why: trade needed a word for where goods begin their journey, and the general sense supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 贸易需要一个词来指货物开始旅程的地方，泛义正好提供了它。

senses.title: The origin of coordinates
senses.definition: the fixed point where the axes of a coordinate system meet
senses.definitionCN: 坐标系各轴相交的固定点
senses.example: The graph starts at the origin and rises to the right.
senses.exampleCN: 图像从原点开始，向右上升。
senses.why: mathematics borrowed the word for the zero point from which all positions are measured.
senses.whyCN: 数学借用了这个词，指一切位置由之量起的零点。

senses.title: The attachment point of a muscle
senses.definition: the end of a muscle that stays fixed when it contracts
senses.definitionCN: 肌肉收缩时保持不动的那一端
senses.example: The muscle's origin is on the pelvis and its insertion on the thigh.
senses.exampleCN: 这块肌肉的起点在骨盆，止点在大腿。
senses.why: anatomy reused the idea of a beginning for the fixed end from which a muscle acts.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学把「开端」的观念用于肌肉发力的固定端。

senses.title: Etymology of a word
senses.definition: the earlier form and language from which a word derives
senses.definitionCN: 一个词所由来的更早形式与语言
senses.example: The dictionary gives the origin of the word in Latin.
senses.exampleCN: 词典给出这个词在拉丁语中的来源。
senses.why: a word's history begins somewhere, and that beginning is literally its origin.
senses.whyCN: 一个词的历史总有个开始，而那个开始字面上就是它的 origin。

senses.title: The first cause of an event
senses.definition: the earliest cause that set a chain of events going
senses.definitionCN: 启动一连串事件的最早原因
senses.example: Investigators traced the fire to an origin in faulty wiring.
senses.exampleCN: 调查者把火灾追溯到有问题的线路。
senses.why: causes form chains, and the first link is naturally called the origin.
senses.whyCN: 原因构成链条，第一环自然被称作 origin。

senses.title: Figurative root or source
senses.definition: a borrowed use for the deepest source of a feeling, problem or custom
senses.definitionCN: 借指情感、问题或习俗的最深根源
senses.example: The origin of their quarrel was a careless remark years before.
senses.exampleCN: 他们争吵的根源是多年前一句无心的话。
senses.why: the physical starting point became the image for whatever lies beneath a visible effect.
senses.whyCN: 物理起点成了可见结果之下一切东西的意象。

intro.en: Origin comes from Latin origo 'beginning, source', from oriri 'to rise'. It entered English through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: origin 来自拉丁 origo「开端、来源」，后者出自动词 oriri「升起」，经法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Oriri meant 'to rise, arise', used of the sun and of anything coming into being. Its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: oriri 意为「升起、出现」，用于太阳与任何开始存在的事物。其更深来源不确定。

items.en: Origo, originis meant 'a beginning, a source, a birth', and supplied the whole family of English words.
items.cn: origo, originis 意为「开端、来源、诞生」，提供了英语整组同族词。

items.en: Old French origine carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first in the sense of a source or birth.
items.cn: 古法语 origine 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，最初指来源或诞生。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the word named the zero point of coordinate axes.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，这个词指坐标轴的零点。

items.en: Anatomy adopted origin for the fixed end of a muscle, extending the family into medicine.
items.cn: 解剖学采用 origin 指肌肉的固定端，把词族扩展到医学。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the pre-Latin source of oriri is not established, and any Indo-European root offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：oriri 在拉丁语之前的来源未得到证明，凡为其提出的印欧词根均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the look-alike nouns built on the same stem; group two holds near-meaning source words.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干构成的形近名词；第二组是语义相近的来源词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'first' or the first version of a work; origin is the starting point itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「最初的」的形容词，或作品的最初版本；origin 是起点本身。

entries.definition: To begin or to bring something into being; it names the event, not the point.
entries.definitionCN: 开始或使某物产生；它指事件，而非那个点。

entries.definition: The quality of being new and inventive; it has moved far from the sense of a beginning.
entries.definitionCN: 新颖而有创造性的品质；已远离「开端」之义。

entries.definition: The process of coming into being; origin is the point, origination is the process.
entries.definitionCN: 产生的过程；origin 是那个点，origination 是过程。

entries.definition: The place, person or thing from which something is obtained; it stresses supply rather than first existence.
entries.definitionCN: 获得某物的地点、人或物；强调供给，而非首次存在。

entries.definition: The first part or first moment of anything; it is the everyday equivalent of origin.
entries.definitionCN: 任何事物的最初部分或最初时刻；是 origin 的日常对应词。

entries.definition: The underlying cause or base of something, often figurative, as the root of a problem.
entries.definitionCN: 事物的深层原因或基础，常为比喻，如问题的根源。

entries.definition: The place where a person or movement was born; it is concrete and geographical.
entries.definitionCN: 人或运动诞生之地；具体且地理性的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin pieces and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁成分与真实固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: oriri 'to rise' plus -go gives 'a rising, a beginning'.
normal.cn: oriri「升起」加 -go 即「升起、开端」。

normal.en: The family runs origin, originate, original, originality, originator.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 origin、originate、original、originality、originator。

normal.en: Country of origin is a fixed trade phrase.
normal.cn: 原产国是固定的贸易短语。

normal.en: The origin of coordinates is the zero point of the axes.
normal.cn: 坐标原点是各轴的零点。

normal.en: Anatomy uses origin for the fixed end of a muscle.
normal.cn: 解剖学用 origin 指肌肉的固定端。

abstract.en: Picture the first thread of water coming out of a rock.
abstract.cn: 想象第一缕水从岩石缝里冒出来。

abstract.en: Picture a family tree whose lowest branch is a village.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵家谱树，最下面的枝条是一个村庄。

abstract.en: Picture a quarrel that began with one careless sentence years ago.
abstract.cn: 想象一场争吵，始于多年前一句无心的话。

examples.en: The origin of the custom is lost.
examples.cn: 这一习俗的起源已经失传。

examples.en: The map marks the origin of every shipment.
examples.cn: 地图标出每批货物的来源地。

examples.en: The graph crosses the origin at zero.
examples.cn: 图像在零点穿过原点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ori（升起）+ gin（开端）」——事物升起来的那个点 → 起源、起点

root: 拉丁 origo, originis「开端、来源」，来自 oriri「升起」；oriri 更深来源不确定，其印欧词根一说属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one rising point: where a thing begins, where a family begins, where goods come from, the zero of axes, the fixed end of a muscle, a word's history, the first cause and the hidden root.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个「升起的点」：事物开始处、家族开始处、货物来处、坐标零点、肌肉固定端、词的历史、最初原因与隐藏根源。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first thread of water rising out of a rock and widening into a river.
core.cn: 核心意象：第一缕水从石缝里升起，逐渐变宽成一条河。

branches.en: BEGINNING AND CAUSE: the first moment and the first cause share one shape.
branches.cn: 开端与原因：最初时刻与最初原因共享同一形状。

branches.en: FAMILY: a person's beginning is a place and a lineage.
branches.cn: 家族：人的开始既是地点，也是血脉。

branches.en: PROVENANCE: goods and words both come from somewhere.
branches.cn: 来源：货物与词都从某处来。

branches.en: FIXED POINTS: axes and muscles need a point that does not move.
branches.cn: 固定点：坐标轴与肌肉都需要一个不动的点。

branches.en: ROOT: the hidden source beneath a visible effect.
branches.cn: 根源：可见结果之下的隐藏来源。

intro.en: Origin is a Latin noun whose stem recurs through a large English family.
intro.cn: origin 是一个拉丁名词，其词干贯穿一大组英语同族词。

latinIntro.en: Oriri 'to rise' gives origo, originis and the English family origin, originate, original and originality.
latinIntro.cn: oriri「升起」给出 origo、originis，以及英语同族 origin、originate、original 与 originality。

items.structure: oriri, ortus sum (Latin verb, fourth conjugation)
items.example: The sun is said to rise with this verb.
items.exampleCN: 太阳「升起」就用这个动词。

items.example: Origo is the direct source of origin.
items.exampleCN: origo 是 origin 的直接来源。

items.example: The origin of the word is Latin.
items.exampleCN: 这个词的来源是拉丁语。

items.example: The practice originated in the north.
The original plan was simpler.
The site was originally an orchard.
Her originality showed in every page.
items.exampleCN: 她的独创性在每一页都显现。

items.example: The originator of the method is unknown.
items.exampleCN: 这一方法的创始者不明。

items.example: The word describes peoples from the beginning.
items.exampleCN: 这个词描述「从一开始就在」的民族。

definition_zh: 形成；形成物；地层；编队；构词
definition_en: the process of coming into being or being arranged, or the thing, group or layer so formed
core_image: 沙与泥一层层落进浅水，压实成层，层与层之间留着清楚的界线
scene: 河口的浅滩上，泥砂一层压着一层，地质队员往下挖，看到界线分明。The formation of the delta took thousands of years of quiet deposition.
sceneCN: 这里指「逐渐形成的过程」（第 1 个义项：事物由零散材料累积成形的过程）；句意为这片三角洲的形成经历了数千年的平静沉积。图中可辨识物件：浅滩、层理、地质锤、剖面。

pos.zh: 形成；形成物；地层；编队；构词

derivatives.zh: 起形成作用的；成长期的

senses.title: The process of taking shape
senses.definition: the process by which something comes into being or takes a definite shape
senses.definitionCN: 事物产生或形成确定形状的过程
senses.example: The formation of the delta took thousands of years of quiet deposition.
senses.exampleCN: 这片三角洲的形成经历了数千年的平静沉积。
senses.why: formatio in Latin named a shaping, from formare 'to shape', so the noun names the act before the result.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 formatio 指「塑形」，来自 formare「塑形」，因此这个名词先命名动作，后命名结果。

senses.title: A thing that has been formed
senses.definition: an object or structure produced by a process of shaping
senses.definitionCN: 由塑形过程产生的物体或结构
senses.example: The strange formation on the cliff looks like a stack of plates.
senses.exampleCN: 崖上那处奇特构造看起来像一摞盘子。
senses.why: the result noun grew from the action noun by the ordinary shift from doing to what is done.
senses.whyCN: 结果名词由动作名词按「做」到「所做之物」的常规转移而来。

senses.title: A geological formation
senses.definition: a body of rock with a common origin and history, mapped as a unit
senses.definitionCN: 具有共同成因与历史、作为单位测绘的一套岩体
senses.example: The formation contains fossils from a shallow sea.
senses.exampleCN: 这套地层含有浅海化石。
senses.why: geology needed a word for a shaped body of rock, and the general result sense fitted exactly.
senses.whyCN: 地质学需要一个词指成形的岩体，泛结果义正好吻合。

senses.title: A military or sports formation
senses.definition: an ordered arrangement of troops, aircraft or players
senses.definitionCN: 部队、飞机或队员的有序排列
senses.example: The squadron flew in a tight formation.
senses.exampleCN: 中队以紧密编队飞行。
senses.why: an arranged group is literally a shape made by placing units, so the noun covered ordered bodies of people too.
senses.whyCN: 被安排好的群体字面上就是由单位摆出的形状，因此这个名词也覆盖有序的人群。

senses.title: A newly organized body
senses.definition: an organization or unit that has recently been brought together
senses.definitionCN: 近期被组建起来的组织或单位
senses.example: The new formation was given its own budget.
senses.exampleCN: 这个新组建的单位获得了自己的预算。
senses.why: from military arrangements the word spread to any body constituted for a purpose.
senses.whyCN: 从军事编排出发，这个词扩展到任何为某一目的组建的团体。

senses.title: Word formation
senses.definition: the process by which new words are built from existing material
senses.definitionCN: 用现有材料构造新词的过程
senses.example: Compounds are one kind of word formation.
senses.exampleCN: 复合是构词的一种方式。
senses.why: linguistics treats words as things shaped from parts, so the shaping noun serves the field.
senses.whyCN: 语言学把词看作由部件塑成之物，因此这个「塑形」名词正好服务该领域。

senses.title: The shape of an arrangement
senses.definition: the visible pattern produced by placing things in a particular order
senses.definitionCN: 把事物按特定次序摆放后产生的可见图案
senses.example: The stars make a familiar formation in the winter sky.
senses.exampleCN: 这些星在冬夜天空中组成熟悉的形状。
senses.why: the visual result of arrangement is a form, and formation names the result as well as the making.
senses.whyCN: 排列的视觉结果是形态，而 formation 既指造就也指结果。

senses.title: Figurative structure or pattern
senses.definition: a borrowed use for the settled pattern of habits, ideas or relations
senses.definitionCN: 借指习惯、观念或关系形成的稳定格局
senses.example: The formation of public opinion takes years, not weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 舆论格局的形成需要数年，而非数周。
senses.why: anything that gradually takes a shape can be spoken of with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 任何逐渐取得形状的东西，都能用同一个词来说。

intro.en: Formation comes from Latin formatio 'a shaping', from formare 'to shape', from forma 'form'. It entered English through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: formation 来自拉丁 formatio「塑形」，来自 formare「塑形」，再来自 forma「形状」，经法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Forma meant 'form, shape, mould'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the link sometimes suggested to Greek morphe 'shape' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: forma 意为「形状、形态、模子」。其更深来源不确定；有人提出与希腊语 morphe「形状」的联系，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Formare 'to shape, mould, form' turned the noun into a verb of making.
items.cn: formare「塑形、造形」把名词变成表「造就」的动词。

items.en: Formatio, formationis named the act of shaping and also the shape produced.
items.cn: formatio, formationis 既指塑形的动作，也指产生的形状。

items.en: Old French formation brought the noun into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 formation 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语。

items.en: Military formation appeared in the seventeenth century and geological formation in the eighteenth, each narrowing the general sense.
items.cn: 军事编队义出现在十七世纪，地质地层义出现在十八世纪，两者都收窄了泛义。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): forma has no established Indo-European ancestor, and the Greek connection often repeated for it is unproven.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：forma 没有已确定的印欧祖先，常被重复的希腊语联系亦未得到证明。

note.en: Group one holds the look-alike nouns from the form family; group two holds near-meaning words for coming into being.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 form 词族的形近名词；第二组是表示「产生」的近义词。

entries.definition: The shape itself or the verb meaning to shape; formation is the process or the resulting body.
entries.definitionCN: 形状本身，或表示塑形的动词；formation 是过程或所成之物。

entries.definition: Describing something that shapes or develops something else, especially in early life.
entries.definitionCN: 描述对别的事物起塑形或发展作用的，尤指早年。

entries.definition: The quality of following strict social rules; it has nothing to do with physical shaping.
entries.definitionCN: 遵守严格社会规则的性质；与物理塑形无关。

entries.definition: The act of expressing something in precise words or of preparing a mixture.
entries.definitionCN: 用精确语言表达某事，或配制混合物的动作。

entries.definition: The act of making something new; it stresses novelty, while formation stresses shaping existing material.
entries.definitionCN: 造出新事物的动作；强调新颖，而 formation 强调对既有材料的塑形。

entries.definition: Gradual growth or change toward a fuller state, often over time and in stages.
entries.definitionCN: 逐渐向更完整状态成长或变化，常跨时间与阶段。

entries.definition: The arrangement of parts in a whole; formation can mean the process that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分在一个整体中的排列；formation 可指产生它的过程。

entries.definition: The act of setting up an institution or the institution itself; more administrative than formation.
entries.definitionCN: 建立机构的行为或机构本身；比 formation 更带行政意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin pieces and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁成分与真实固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: forma 'shape' plus -atio 'action' gives 'a shaping'.
normal.cn: forma「形状」加 -atio「动作」即「塑形」。

normal.en: The family runs form, formation, formative, formal, format.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 form、formation、formative、formal、format。

normal.en: Rock formation and military formation are two narrowings of one idea.
normal.cn: 岩层与军事编队是同一观念的两个收窄。

normal.en: Word formation treats words as built from parts.
normal.cn: 构词研究把词看作由部件造成。

normal.en: The noun can mean either the process or the thing produced.
normal.cn: 这个名词既可指过程，也可指所成之物。

abstract.en: Picture silt settling layer by layer until a bank appears.
abstract.cn: 想象泥沙一层层落下，直到出现一道滩。

abstract.en: Picture soldiers arranging themselves into a visible shape.
abstract.cn: 想象士兵把自己排成一个看得见的形状。

abstract.en: Picture an opinion hardening slowly into a settled pattern.
abstract.cn: 想象一种看法慢慢凝成稳定格局。

examples.en: The formation of the canyon exposed millions of years of layers.
examples.cn: 峡谷的形成露出了数百万年的层理。

examples.en: The team lined up in a defensive formation.
examples.cn: 球队排成防守阵形。

examples.en: Word formation explains how compounds are built.
examples.cn: 构词解释了复合词如何构成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「form（形状）+ ation（动作）」——把东西塑出形状这一动作及其结果 → 形成、构造、编队

root: 拉丁 forma「形状」→ formare「塑形」→ formatio「塑形」；forma 更深来源不确定，与希腊 morphe「形状」的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shaping: a process, its product, a rock body, an ordered troop, a new unit, a word, a visible pattern and a settled structure.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一次塑形：过程、产物、岩体、有序队伍、新单位、词、可见图案与稳定结构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: silt settling layer upon layer until a firm bank with visible lines appears.
core.cn: 核心意象：泥沙一层层落下，直到出现带清晰层线的坚实滩岸。

branches.en: PROCESS: from a physical shaping to a slowly settled pattern.
branches.cn: 过程：从物理塑形到缓慢定型的格局。

branches.en: SHAPED BODY: a result that can be mapped and named.
branches.cn: 成形之物：可被测绘并命名的结果。

branches.en: ARRANGEMENT: people and stars make visible shapes.
branches.cn: 排列：人与星都摆出可见的形状。

branches.en: INSTITUTION: a group constituted as a unit.
branches.cn: 机构：作为一个单位组建起来的群体。

branches.en: LANGUAGE: words themselves are shaped from parts.
branches.cn: 语言：词本身也由部件塑成。

intro.en: Formation is a Latin action noun whose base, verb and suffix all remain productive in English.
intro.cn: formation 是拉丁动作名词，其词基、动词与后缀在英语中仍有能产性。

latinIntro.en: Forma 'shape' gives formare 'to shape' and formatio 'a shaping'; -atio marks an action or its result.
latinIntro.cn: forma「形状」给出 formare「塑形」与 formatio「塑形」；-atio 标记动作或其结果。

items.example: Forma is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: forma 是这个词族的词基。

items.example: The verb names the act of shaping.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指塑形的动作。

items.example: The suffix builds action nouns.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成动作名词。

items.meaning: a shaping or what is shaped
items.example: The formation took centuries.
items.exampleCN: 这一形成过程历经数百年。

items.example: The clay kept its form.
The formative years were quiet.
The fog was formless.
The letter was formal.

items.meaning: the shape of a page or file
items.example: The file format changed.
The formulation was carefully worded.

definition_zh: 行星形成；行星由原行星盘物质聚集而成的过程与理论
definition_en: the process by which planets grow from the gas and dust of a protoplanetary disk, or the study of that process
core_image: 一圈尘埃与气体绕着年轻恒星旋转，颗粒粘成越来越大的团块
scene: 年轻恒星周围的原行星盘里，尘埃颗粒在碰撞中粘成小团，又滚成大团，最后清出一条条环缝。Planetary formation begins in a disk of gas and dust around a young star.
sceneCN: 这里指「行星由原行星盘中的尘埃与气体聚集形成的整个过程」（第 1 个义项：行星从微小颗粒长成行星体的过程）；句意为行星形成始于年轻恒星周围由气体与尘埃构成的盘。图中可辨识物件：原行星盘、尘埃颗粒、环缝、年轻恒星。

pos.zh: 行星形成（不可数；具体模型可数，复数为 planetary formations）

collocations.zh: 双星系统中的行星形成

senses.title: The process of building planets
senses.definition: the process by which solid planets grow from dust and gas in a disk around a young star
senses.definitionCN: 固体行星由年轻恒星周围盘中的尘埃与气体生长出来的过程
senses.example: Planetary formation begins in a disk of gas and dust around a young star.
senses.exampleCN: 行星形成始于年轻恒星周围由气体与尘埃构成的盘。
senses.why: planetary supplies the object and formation supplies the shaping process, so the phrase names how planets come to be.
senses.whyCN: planetary 提供对象，formation 提供塑形过程，因此这个短语指行星如何生成。

senses.title: The theory or model of the process
senses.titleCN: 行星形成的理论或模型
senses.definition: the body of theory that explains how planets assemble
senses.definitionCN: 解释行星如何聚集而成的理论总体
senses.example: The standard model of planetary formation has been revised for close-in giants.
senses.exampleCN: 针对近距离巨行星，行星形成的标准模型已被修正。
senses.why: a process noun readily becomes the name of the science that studies it.
senses.whyCN: 过程名词很容易转而指研究该过程的科学。

senses.title: The protoplanetary disk stage
senses.definition: the early stage in which a rotating disk of gas and dust surrounds the young star
senses.definitionCN: 气体与尘埃组成的旋转盘围绕年轻恒星的早期阶段
senses.example: Planetary formation starts with a disk that lasts only a few million years.
senses.exampleCN: 行星形成始于一个只持续数百万年的盘。
senses.why: the phrase can mark the setting as well as the whole process, since the disk is where it happens.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语既可标记整个过程，也可标记其发生场所，因为盘正是事情发生的地方。

senses.title: Accretion by planetesimals
senses.definition: the growth of larger bodies by collisions among smaller solid bodies
senses.definitionCN: 较小固体天体碰撞而使较大天体成长
senses.example: Planetary formation depends on planetesimals sticking together rather than bouncing apart.
senses.exampleCN: 行星形成取决于星子粘合而不是弹开。
senses.why: the mechanism that turns dust into planets is accretion, and the phrase names the episode it drives.
senses.whyCN: 把尘埃变成行星的机制是吸积，而这一短语命名它所推动的阶段。

senses.title: The timescale of planet building
senses.definition: the span of time required for planets to assemble
senses.definitionCN: 行星聚集所需的时间跨度
senses.example: Planetary formation is fast in astronomical terms, yet still takes millions of years.
senses.exampleCN: 按天文学标准，行星形成很快，但仍需数百万年。
senses.why: formation carries an implied duration, so the phrase can be used to discuss how long the process takes.
senses.whyCN: formation 本身隐含一段时间跨度，因此这个短语可用于讨论过程持续多久。

senses.title: Exoplanet formation research
senses.definition: the branch that studies how planets form around other stars
senses.definitionCN: 研究其他恒星周围行星如何形成的分支
senses.example: Planetary formation research now compares hundreds of known systems.
senses.exampleCN: 行星形成研究如今比较数百个已知系统。
senses.why: the same phrase covers the field as it is practised on exoplanets, not only on the solar system.
senses.whyCN: 同一短语也覆盖在系外行星上开展的该领域，而不只限于太阳系。

senses.title: The solar system case
senses.definition: the particular history by which the planets of our own system assembled
senses.definitionCN: 我们自己系统中各行星聚集而成的具体历史
senses.example: The solar system is the best-studied case of planetary formation.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳系是研究得最清楚的行星形成实例。
senses.why: the phrase names both the general process and the one historical instance we can examine closely.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语既指一般过程，也指我们能近距离考察的那一次历史实例。

senses.title: Figurative slow assembly from dust
senses.titleCN: 借喻：由尘埃慢慢聚成新体系
senses.definition: a borrowed use for any large structure that is assembled slowly from tiny parts
senses.definitionCN: 借指任何由微小部件缓慢聚成的大结构
senses.example: The committee's planetary formation took a decade of small meetings.
senses.exampleCN: 这个委员会的「行星形成」用了十年小会。
senses.why: the cosmic image of dust becoming worlds suits any slow aggregation of small pieces.
senses.whyCN: 尘埃变成世界的宇宙意象，适合任何由小件缓慢聚集的过程。

intro.en: Planetary formation joins Greek planetes 'wanderer' with Latin formatio 'a shaping'. The modern technical sense is twentieth-century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: planetary formation 把希腊 planetes「漫游者」与拉丁 formatio「塑形」连接起来；现代技术义属二十世纪。年代均为约数。

items.en: Planetes meant 'wanderer', from planasthai 'to wander', because the planets move against the fixed stars.
items.cn: planetes 意为「漫游者」，来自 planasthai「漫游」，因为行星在恒星背景上移动。

items.en: Late Latin planeta carried the Greek word into European languages, and English planet followed through French.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 planeta 把希腊词带入欧洲各语言，英语 planet 经法语而来。

items.en: Formare 'to shape' plus -atio gave formatio 'a shaping', which became English formation.
items.cn: formare「塑形」加 -atio 构成 formatio「塑形」，进入英语作 formation。

items.en: The nebular and planetesimal theories of the eighteenth to twentieth centuries gave the phrase its technical content.
items.cn: 十八至二十世纪的星云说与星子说赋予这个短语技术内容。

items.en: After the 1990s the phrase expanded to cover planets around other stars, not only the solar system.
items.cn: 二十世纪九十年代以后，这个短语扩展到其他恒星周围的行星，而不只太阳系。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the pre-Greek source of planasthai is unsettled, and Latin forma has no established Indo-European ancestor.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：planasthai 在希腊语之前的来源无定论，拉丁 forma 也没有已确定的印欧祖先。

note.en: Group one holds the look-alike formation terms in astronomy; group two holds near-meaning growth words.
note.cn: 第一组是天文学中形近的形成术语；第二组是语义相近的生长词。

entries.definition: The same process named with the noun planet instead of its adjective; it is the common informal wording.
entries.definitionCN: 同一过程，用名词 planet 代替形容词命名；是常见的非正式说法。

entries.definition: The growth of a body by adding material; accretion is one step inside planetary formation, not the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 天体通过添加物质而成长；吸积是行星形成中的一个步骤，而非全过程。

entries.definition: A shell of gas thrown off by a dying star; the adjective planetary here is historical and misleading.
entries.definitionCN: 垂死恒星抛出的气体壳；这里的形容词 planetary 是历史遗留且易误导。

entries.definition: A small planet-like body; it is a product of the process, not the process itself.
entries.definitionCN: 类行星的小天体；是过程的产物，而非过程本身。

entries.definition: Any process of taking shape; planetary formation is the astronomical case.
entries.definitionCN: 任何成形的过程；行星形成是天文学中的情形。

entries.definition: The act of fitting parts into a whole, often mechanical or deliberate.
entries.definitionCN: 把部件装成整体的动作，常为机械或有意的。

entries.definition: Increase in size or mass, the result the process produces in a young planet.
entries.definitionCN: 尺寸或质量的增加，是过程在年轻行星上产生的结果。

entries.definition: A formal word for origin, often used of a whole class of objects.
entries.definitionCN: 表示起源的正式词，常用于一整类对象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek and Latin pieces, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊与拉丁成分，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: planet comes from a Greek word for wanderer.
normal.cn: planet 来自希腊语中表示「漫游者」的词。

normal.en: formation is a shaping, so the phrase means the shaping of planets.
normal.cn: formation 是塑形，因此短语意为行星的塑成。

normal.en: Dust sticks into planetesimals, planetesimals collide into protoplanets.
normal.cn: 尘埃粘成星子，星子撞成原行星。

normal.en: The disk lasts only a few million years, so the process must be quick.
normal.cn: 盘只持续数百万年，因此过程必须很快。

normal.en: The solar system is the best-studied case.
normal.cn: 太阳系是研究得最清楚的实例。

abstract.en: Picture grains in a ring colliding until one lump wins.
abstract.cn: 想象环中的颗粒相撞，直到某个团块胜出。

abstract.en: Picture a young star sweeping clear lanes through its own dust.
abstract.cn: 想象年轻恒星在自己的尘埃里扫出空道。

abstract.en: Picture a committee slowly accreting members and rules.
abstract.cn: 想象一个委员会慢慢吸积成员与规则。

examples.en: Planetary formation models struggle with how giants avoid spiralling inward.
examples.cn: 行星形成模型难以解释巨行星如何避免向内旋落。

examples.en: The telescope observed a disk in the middle of planetary formation.
examples.cn: 望远镜观测到一个正处于行星形成中的盘。

examples.en: Planetary formation in binary systems may differ from the solar case.
examples.cn: 双星系统中的行星形成可能与太阳系情形不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「planetary（行星的）+ formation（形成）」——行星怎样被塑出来 → 行星形成

root: 希腊 planetes「漫游者」（来自 planasthai「漫游」）+ 拉丁 forma「形状」→ formare「塑形」→ formatio「塑形」。planasthai 与 forma 的更深来源均不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one assembly: the process, its theory, the disk, accretion, its timescale, exoplanet research, the solar case and finally any slow aggregation of small parts.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一次聚集：过程、理论、盘、吸积、时标、系外研究、太阳系实例，最后是任何小件缓慢聚成整体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ring of dust around a young star, grains sticking into larger and larger lumps.
core.cn: 核心意象：年轻恒星周围的尘埃环，颗粒粘成越来越大的团块。

branches.en: PROCESS AND THEORY: the event and the account of it.
branches.cn: 过程与理论：事件本身，以及关于它的叙述。

branches.en: THE DISK: the setting that supplies the material.
branches.cn: 盘：提供材料的场所。

branches.en: ACCRETION AND TIME: how the material adds up, and how long it takes.
branches.cn: 吸积与时间：材料怎样累加，以及需要多久。

branches.en: OTHER STARS AND OUR OWN: the general field and the local case.
branches.cn: 别的恒星与我们自己：一般领域与本地实例。

branches.en: FIGURATIVE ASSEMBLY: any large structure built slowly from small parts.
branches.cn: 比喻的聚集：任何由小件缓慢建成的大结构。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek noun of wandering to a Latin noun of shaping, so both halves carry separate families.
intro.cn: 这个短语把希腊语中表「漫游」的名词与拉丁语中表「塑形」的名词连接起来，两半各有词族。

latinIntro.en: Greek planetes and planasthai supply the first half; Latin forma, formare and formatio supply the second, with planeta as the Latinized bridge.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 planetes 与 planasthai 提供前半；拉丁 forma、formare 与 formatio 提供后半，planeta 是拉丁化的桥梁。

items.example: Planetes explains why planets were named for wandering.
items.exampleCN: planetes 解释了行星为何以「漫游」命名。

items.example: The verb lies behind planetes.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词在 planetes 背后。

items.example: The planet orbits a young star.
items.exampleCN: 这颗行星绕一颗年轻恒星运行。

items.example: Planetary science is a growing field.
items.exampleCN: 行星科学是一个成长中的领域。

items.meaning: a small solid building block of planets
items.example: Planetesimals collide and merge.
A protoplanet clears its orbit.
items.exampleCN: 原行星清空自己的轨道。

items.example: Formation names the process.
The disk has a flattened form.
The formative stage lasts briefly.

items.meaning: a planet beyond the solar system
items.example: Exoplanets widened the field.
items.exampleCN: 系外行星拓宽了这一领域。

latinEntries.structure: planeta, planetae (m., first declension, from Greek)

definition_en: the act of turning about an axis, one complete turn, or a regular succession in which people or crops take turns
core_image: 磨盘绕中间的轴不停转动，轴心不动，谷粒从孔里落下被碾开
scene: 磨坊里，石磨绕中间的轴转，谷物从孔里落进去，被磨成粉从边缘出来。The rotation of the millstone crushed the grain in a single pass.
sceneCN: 这里指「绕轴转动的运动」（第 1 个义项：物体绕自身或外部轴心旋转）；句意为磨盘的转动一趟就把谷物碾碎。图中可辨识物件：石磨、中轴、谷粒、出粉口。

pos.zh: 旋转；自转；一次转动；轮换；轮作

senses.title: Turning about an axis
senses.definition: the movement of a body turning around a fixed axis
senses.definitionCN: 物体绕固定轴转动的运动
senses.example: The rotation of the millstone crushed the grain in a single pass.
senses.exampleCN: 磨盘的转动一趟就把谷物碾碎。
senses.why: rotatio in Latin named a turning, from rotare 'to turn' and rota 'wheel', so the noun begins as pure motion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 rotatio 指「转动」，来自 rotare「转」与 rota「轮」，因此这个名词最初就是纯运动。

senses.title: One complete turn
senses.definition: a single complete turn through three hundred and sixty degrees
senses.definitionCN: 转满三百六十度的一整圈
senses.example: The handle needs one full rotation to open the valve.
senses.exampleCN: 手柄需要转一整圈才能打开阀门。
senses.why: counting turns turned the process noun into a countable unit of angle.
senses.whyCN: 数圈数的需要，把过程名词变成了可计数的角度单位。

senses.title: Taking turns in order
senses.definition: a regular order in which people or groups take their turn
senses.definitionCN: 人或群体按固定次序轮流承担
senses.example: The doctors work in rotation so that someone is always awake.
senses.exampleCN: 医生们轮流值班，以保证总有人醒着。
senses.why: people succeeding one another in a fixed order trace a circle, so the turning image became a scheduling word.
senses.whyCN: 人按固定次序接替，轨迹像一个圆，于是转动的意象成了排班用词。

senses.title: Crop rotation
senses.definition: the practice of growing different crops in a fixed sequence on the same land
senses.definitionCN: 在同一块地上按固定顺序种不同作物的做法
senses.example: Crop rotation kept the soil from wearing out.
senses.exampleCN: 轮作使土壤不致耗尽。
senses.why: fields take their turn in a cycle, so agriculture borrowed the same circular scheduling idea.
senses.whyCN: 田地按周期轮流，农业借用了同一套循环排程观念。

senses.title: The spin of a celestial body
senses.definition: the turning of a planet, star or moon about its own axis
senses.definitionCN: 行星、恒星或卫星绕自身轴的转动
senses.example: The rotation of the earth makes the stars appear to move.
senses.exampleCN: 地球的自转使恒星看起来在移动。
senses.why: astronomy applied the general motion noun to the spin of whole worlds.
senses.whyCN: 天文学把这个泛运动名词用于整个世界的自转。

senses.title: A rotation in mathematics
senses.definition: a transformation that turns a figure about a fixed point by a given angle
senses.definitionCN: 把图形绕定点转过给定角度的变换
senses.example: A rotation of ninety degrees maps the square onto itself.
senses.exampleCN: 旋转九十度把这个正方形映到自身。
senses.why: geometry isolated the pure turn from the turning body and made it an operation.
senses.whyCN: 几何把纯粹的「转」从转动的物体中抽离出来，使之成为一种运算。

senses.title: Job or shift rotation
senses.definition: a system in which workers change duties or shifts on a fixed schedule
senses.definitionCN: 工人按固定时间表更换职责或班次的制度
senses.example: Shift rotation gave everyone a share of the night work.
senses.exampleCN: 班次轮换让每个人都分担夜班。
senses.why: the scheduling sense became an administrative term for fair distribution of work.
senses.whyCN: 排班义成了公平分配工作的管理术语。

senses.title: Figurative cyclical succession
senses.definition: a borrowed use for the regular return of seasons, fashions or generations
senses.definitionCN: 借指季节、风尚或世代的有规律回归
senses.example: The rotation of fashion brought the old coat back again.
senses.exampleCN: 时尚的循环让那件旧外套又回来了。
senses.why: anything that returns in order looks like a wheel turning, so the word serves cycles of every kind.
senses.whyCN: 任何按序回归之物都像轮子在转，因此这个词适用于各种循环。

intro.en: Rotation comes from Latin rotatio 'a turning', from rotare 'to turn', from rota 'wheel'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: rotation 来自拉丁 rotatio「转动」，来自 rotare「转」，再来自 rota「轮」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Rota meant 'wheel'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the link sometimes suggested to a root meaning 'to run or roll' is a reconstruction.
items.cn: rota 意为「轮」。其更深来源不确定；有人提出与意为「跑、滚」的词根有联系，那属重构。

items.en: Rotare meant 'to turn, revolve, rotate', used of wheels, bodies and cycles of time.
items.cn: rotare 意为「转、旋转、回旋」，用于轮子、天体与时间循环。

items.en: Rotatio, rotationis named the act of turning and supplied the English noun.
items.cn: rotatio, rotationis 指转动的动作，提供了英语名词。

items.en: The noun entered English in the sixteenth century, first in astronomy and mechanics.
items.cn: 这个名词在十六世纪进入英语，最初用于天文学与力学。

items.en: Crop rotation spread in the eighteenth century, extending the word from motion to scheduling.
items.cn: 轮作在十八世纪推广，把这个词从运动扩展到排程。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): rota has no established Indo-European ancestor, and the root often printed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：rota 没有已确定的印欧祖先，常为它印出的词根属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the look-alike nouns and adjectives from the same stem; group two holds near-meaning motion words.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干的形近名词与形容词；第二组是语义相近的运动词。

entries.definition: Relating to rotation; the adjective describes a property, while rotation is the motion.
entries.definitionCN: 与旋转有关的；形容词描述性质，而 rotation 是运动。

entries.definition: To turn about an axis or to take turns; it names the action, not the cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 绕轴转动或轮流；它指动作，而非周期。

entries.definition: The part of a machine that turns; it is a component, not the motion.
entries.definitionCN: 机器中转动的部件；是零件，而非运动。

entries.definition: Describing a machine that works by turning, such as a rotary engine.
entries.definitionCN: 描述靠转动工作的机器，如转子发动机。

entries.definition: One complete turn or one orbit around another body; rotation is spin about one's own axis.
entries.definitionCN: 完整的一转，或绕另一天体的公转；rotation 是绕自身轴的自转。

entries.definition: Rapid turning, often with the idea of speed or dizziness; rotation is neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 快速转动，常带速度或眩晕之意；rotation 是中性的。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for one movement around a point or for a place in a sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 绕一点转一次，或序列中一个位置的日常词。

entries.definition: A series that returns to its starting state; rotation stresses the turning motion inside a cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 回到起始状态的序列；rotation 强调循环中的转动。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin pieces and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁成分与真实固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: rota 'wheel' gives rotare 'to turn' and rotatio 'a turning'.
normal.cn: rota「轮」给出 rotare「转」与 rotatio「转动」。

normal.en: The family runs rotate, rotation, rotational, rotor, rotary.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 rotate、rotation、rotational、rotor、rotary。

normal.en: Earth's rotation is spin; its revolution is orbit.
normal.cn: 地球的 rotation 是自转；revolution 是公转。

normal.en: Crop rotation and job rotation both schedule turns.
normal.cn: 轮作与岗位轮换都在安排轮次。

normal.en: In rotation means taking turns in a fixed order.
normal.cn: 固定短语「轮流地」表示按固定次序轮班。

abstract.en: Picture a millstone turning while its centre stays still.
abstract.cn: 想象磨盘转动，中心却不动。

abstract.en: Picture a wheel of seasons returning to the same mark.
abstract.cn: 想象季节之轮回到同一个刻度。

abstract.en: Picture a rota where each name moves one place forward.
abstract.cn: 想象一张轮值表，每个名字向前挪一位。

examples.en: One rotation of the wheel lifts the bucket to the top.
examples.cn: 轮子转一圈就把桶提到顶。

examples.en: The rotation of the staff keeps night shifts fair.
examples.cn: 员工轮换使夜班分配公平。

examples.en: Crop rotation restored nitrogen to the field.
examples.cn: 轮作把氮归还给田地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rot（轮、转）+ ation（动作）」——轮子转起来这一动作 → 旋转、轮换

root: 拉丁 rota「轮」→ rotare「转」→ rotatio「转动」；rota 更深来源不确定，常为其提出的「跑、滚」词根属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one turn: a body about its axis, one full circle, people taking turns, fields taking turns, a planet spinning, a figure mapped onto itself, a shift schedule and any returning cycle.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一次转动：物体绕轴、一整圈、人轮流、田轮作、行星自转、图形映到自身、班次轮换，以及任何回归的循环。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a millstone turning around a fixed axle while the grain is crushed beneath it.
core.cn: 核心意象：磨盘绕固定轴转动，谷物在下面被碾碎。

branches.en: PURE TURN: physical motion and its mathematical abstraction.
branches.cn: 纯粹的转：物理运动及其数学抽象。

branches.en: COUNTED SPIN: one turn of a handle or of a world.
branches.cn: 可数的自转：手柄的一圈，或一个世界的一圈。

branches.en: SCHEDULED TURNS: people and shifts succeed one another.
branches.cn: 排定的轮次：人与班次彼此接替。

branches.en: FIELDS: crops return in a fixed order.
branches.cn: 田地：作物按固定次序回归。

branches.en: CYCLES: seasons, fashions and generations come round again.
branches.cn: 循环：季节、风尚与世代再次转回。

intro.en: Rotation is a Latin action noun from a noun of a wheel, so the whole family turns on one root.
intro.cn: rotation 是由「轮」的名词派生的拉丁动作名词，整个词族围绕一个词根转动。

latinIntro.en: Rota, rotare and rotatio supply rotation, rotate, rotor and rotary; -atio marks the action.
latinIntro.cn: rota、rotare 与 rotatio 提供 rotation、rotate、rotor 与 rotary；-atio 标记动作。

items.example: Rota is the root of the family.
items.exampleCN: rota 是这个词族的词根。

items.example: The verb names the turning.
The suffix makes action nouns.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成动作名词。

items.example: One rotation takes a day.
The staff rotate each week.
Rotational speed is measured in radians.
The rotor spins inside the coil.
A rotary engine has no pistons.
The rotator holds the sample steady.

definition_zh: 旋转的；转动的；轮作的；轮值的
definition_en: relating to rotation, or organized as a regular succession of turns
core_image: 一根长轴带着几个轮子同速转动，轮缘上的标记划过同一角度
scene: 车间里，一根长轴带着几个轮子同速转动，轮缘上的标记划过同一角度。The rotational speed of the shaft is measured in revolutions per minute.
sceneCN: 这里指「与旋转有关的」（第 1 个义项：属于绕轴转动的）；句意为这根轴的转速以每分钟转数来计量。图中可辨识物件：长轴、轮子、轮缘标记、转速表。

pos.zh: 旋转的；转动的；轮作的；轮值的

senses.title: Relating to turning about an axis
senses.definition: connected with movement around an axis
senses.definitionCN: 与绕轴运动有关的
senses.example: The rotational speed of the shaft is measured in revolutions per minute.
senses.exampleCN: 这根轴的转速以每分钟转数来计量。
senses.why: -al turns the noun rotation into an adjective of relation, so the word simply means 'of rotation'.
senses.whyCN: -al 把名词 rotation 变成表关系的形容词，因此这个词就是「旋转的」。

senses.title: Rotational motion in physics
senses.definition: the motion of a body that turns about an axis rather than translating
senses.definitionCN: 物体绕轴转动而非平移的运动
senses.example: Rotational motion obeys its own equations in mechanics.
senses.exampleCN: 转动在力学中遵守自己的方程。
senses.why: physics separates turning from sliding, and the adjective marks the turning branch.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把转动与平动分开，形容词标记转动这一分支。

senses.title: Rotational symmetry
senses.definition: the property of a shape that looks the same after being turned by some angle
senses.definitionCN: 图形转过某个角度后看起来不变的性质
senses.example: A snowflake has sixfold rotational symmetry.
senses.exampleCN: 雪花具有六重旋转对称。
senses.why: symmetry is defined by operations, and the adjective names the operation that leaves the figure unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 对称由操作定义，形容词命名那个使图形保持不变的操作。

senses.title: Rotational speed
senses.definition: the rate at which something turns, measured in turns or radians per unit time
senses.definitionCN: 转动快慢的速率，以单位时间的圈数或弧度计
senses.example: The rotational speed doubled when the load was removed.
senses.exampleCN: 卸去负载后转速翻倍。
senses.why: the adjective fixes speed as angular rather than linear speed.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把速度限定为角速度，而非线速度。

senses.title: Rotational inertia
senses.definition: the resistance of a body to a change in its rotation, depending on mass and its distribution
senses.definitionCN: 物体抵抗转动改变的性质，取决于质量及其分布
senses.example: A longer rod has greater rotational inertia.
senses.exampleCN: 更长的杆具有更大的转动惯量。
senses.why: inertia in a straight line becomes inertia in a turn, and the adjective marks that version.
senses.whyCN: 直线运动中的惯性变成转动中的惯性，形容词标记这一版本。

senses.title: Rotational grazing or cropping
senses.definition: organized so that animals or crops move through a fixed sequence of fields
senses.definitionCN: 按固定顺序让牲畜或作物在各块田地上轮转
senses.example: Rotational grazing gave each pasture time to recover.
senses.exampleCN: 轮牧给每片草场恢复的时间。
senses.why: the scheduling sense of rotation takes the adjective when the arrangement is a fixed cycle.
senses.whyCN: rotation 的排程义在指固定周期安排时取形容词形式。

senses.title: Rotational shift or duty
senses.definition: arranged so that people take duties in a regular order
senses.definitionCN: 按固定次序让人承担职责的安排
senses.example: The rotational shift system was hard on sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 轮班制度对睡眠很不友好。
senses.why: the adjective marks an administrative cycle rather than a physical turn.
senses.whyCN: 形容词标记一种管理性周期，而非物理转动。

senses.title: Figurative cyclical
senses.definition: a borrowed use for any process that returns in a regular cycle
senses.definitionCN: 借指任何按规律循环回归的过程
senses.example: The rotational pattern of the seasons shaped the festival.
senses.exampleCN: 季节的循环格局塑成了这个节庆。
senses.why: the turning adjective extends from machines to any recurring order.
senses.whyCN: 这个表转动的形容词从机械扩展到任何往复的秩序。

intro.en: Rotational is rotation plus the Latin-French relational suffix -al. The base comes from Latin rota 'wheel'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: rotational 是 rotation 加拉丁—法语来源的关系后缀 -al；词基来自拉丁 rota「轮」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Rota meant 'wheel'; its deeper origin is uncertain, and the root often proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: rota 意为「轮」；其更深来源不确定，常为其提出的词根属重构。

items.en: Rotare 'to turn' produced rotatio 'a turning', the noun behind rotation.
items.cn: rotare「转」产生 rotatio「转动」，即 rotation 背后的名词。

items.en: The relational suffix -al came through Latin -alis and French, and turns nouns into adjectives of belonging.
items.cn: 关系后缀 -al 经拉丁 -alis 与法语而来，把名词变成表归属的形容词。

items.en: Rotational motion, inertia and speed became standard in mechanics from the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.
items.cn: 转动、转动惯量与转速从十八、十九世纪起成为力学标准术语。

items.en: Rotational grazing and rotational shifts extended the adjective to scheduling in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 轮牧与轮班在二十世纪把这个形容词扩展到排班。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): rota has no established Indo-European ancestor, and the root usually cited for it is reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：rota 没有已确定的印欧祖先，通常为它引用的词根属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the look-alike forms of the same family; group two holds near-meaning adjectives.
note.cn: 第一组是同词族的形近形式；第二组是语义相近的形容词。

entries.definition: The motion or the cycle itself; the adjective only describes something as belonging to it.
entries.definitionCN: 运动或周期本身；形容词只描述某物属于它。

entries.definition: Describing a machine that turns in operation; it is narrower than rotational.
entries.definitionCN: 描述运转时转动的机器；比 rotational 更窄。

entries.definition: To turn or to take turns; the verb names the action the adjective describes.
entries.definitionCN: 转动或轮流；动词指形容词所描述的动作。

entries.definition: An older adjective for turning machinery, now largely replaced by rotary and rotational.
entries.definitionCN: 指转动机械的较旧形容词，如今多由 rotary 与 rotational 取代。

entries.definition: Relating to angles; angular speed is the quantity that rotational speed measures.
entries.definitionCN: 与角度有关；角速度正是转速所测的量。

entries.definition: Shaped like a circle; a circular path can be produced by rotation but is not rotation itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形状像圆；圆形路径可由旋转产生，但并非旋转本身。

entries.definition: Turning quickly at a moment; it is more dynamic and less technical than rotational.
entries.definitionCN: 此刻快速转动；比 rotational 更有动感、更少技术性。

entries.definition: Moving around a centre, often on an orbit; rotation is about an internal axis.
entries.definitionCN: 绕中心运动，常指轨道；rotation 是绕自身轴。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real physics terms and real schedules, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实后缀、真实物理术语与真实排班，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Rotation plus -al makes the relational adjective.
normal.cn: rotation 加 -al 构成关系形容词。

normal.en: Rotational speed is angular speed; linear speed is a different quantity.
normal.cn: 转速是角速度；线速度是另一个量。

normal.en: Rotational symmetry is tested by turning the figure.
normal.cn: 旋转对称靠转动图形来检验。

normal.en: Rotational grazing and rotational shifts both schedule turns.
normal.cn: 轮牧与轮班都在安排轮次。

normal.en: Rotary describes a machine; rotational describes the property.
normal.cn: rotary 描述机器；rotational 描述性质。

abstract.en: Picture a long shaft carrying several wheels at one speed.
abstract.cn: 想象一根长轴带着几个轮子同速转动。

abstract.en: Picture a snowflake unchanged after one sixth of a turn.
abstract.cn: 想象雪花转过六分之一圈后毫无变化。

abstract.en: Picture a duty list that comes round to your name again.
abstract.cn: 想象值班表又轮回到你的名字。

examples.en: Rotational inertia explains why the skater pulls her arms in.
examples.cn: 转动惯量解释了滑冰者为何收臂。

examples.en: The machine's rotational speed is kept below its limit.
examples.cn: 机器的转速被保持在限值以下。

examples.en: The farm uses rotational grazing across six paddocks.
examples.cn: 这家农场在六块围场间轮牧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rotation（旋转）+ -al（……的）」——与旋转有关的、绕轴转动的

root: rotation + -al；rotation 来自拉丁 rota「轮」→ rotare「转」→ rotatio「转动」；rota 更深来源不确定，其词根一说属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one relational adjective: the axis, the physics, symmetry, speed, inertia, grazing, shifts and any recurring cycle.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个关系形容词：轴、物理、对称、转速、惯量、轮牧、轮班，以及任何往复循环。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one long shaft carrying several wheels, every rim mark sweeping the same angle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根长轴带着几个轮子，每个轮缘标记扫过同一角度。

branches.en: RELATION AND MOTION: the adjective and the branch of mechanics it marks.
branches.cn: 关系与运动：形容词，以及它所标记的力学分支。

branches.en: SYMMETRY: turning a figure leaves it unchanged.
branches.cn: 对称：转动图形而它不变。

branches.en: SPEED AND RESISTANCE: how fast it turns and how hard it is to change.
branches.cn: 快慢与阻力：转得多快，以及改变它有多难。

branches.en: SCHEDULES: fields and workers take turns in a fixed cycle.
branches.cn: 排程：田地与工人按固定周期轮转。

branches.en: CYCLES: any regular return borrows the turning adjective.
branches.cn: 循环：任何规律回归都借用这个表转动的形容词。

intro.en: Rotational is a derived adjective from the Latin wheel family, with a productive relational suffix.
intro.cn: rotational 是从拉丁「轮」词族派生的形容词，带一个能产的关系后缀。

latinIntro.en: Rota and rotare give rotation; -alis gives the adjective ending that English renders as -al.
latinIntro.cn: rota 与 rotare 给出 rotation；-alis 给出形容词词尾，英语作 -al。

items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成关系形容词。

items.example: Rotational motion is angular.
The part is rotationally symmetric.
items.exampleCN: 这个部件具有旋转对称性。
